en: The Sāmaveda Prātiśākhya, known as the Sāmaprātiśākhya,
was composed by Puṣparṣi.

Uccamahī, Punāravajaya, Ātvauśana, Kayādevya, Taṃvordhas, Taroleya, Svādhita, Pavasvendramaccha, Saphakala, Puraḥśyāvāgava, Abhiprikāva, Svāsu, Jñīya, Mehyūsāka, Vayaṃ, Bharamadhārmedha, Pāntahavya, Pravaḥśāktya, and Vayaṅkāṇve—these are the first [of the seers].

*Indra ā kakṣamayan*, *dāsa urdhvasadmānam*, *ātūpāram*, *abhi tvā vṛṣabha*, *idam gāram*, *idam ghṛtam*, *cunnidhanam*, *ātve tithim*, *yoge yoge*, *medhamindra sute*, *kausam*, *āśvaḥ droṇasuta*, *soma ekarcāḥ*, *pra so jayant*, *tr̥ce pra so hitam*, *ayāsyaḥ pham*, *ākṣāraharya*, *pra sunvānāya gauriḥ*, *gautama ekarcāḥ*, *vr̥ṣā yauktādyam*, *punāyāsyamaiḍe dvitīyaḥ*.

In these very [verses], one should chant the *triṇidhana* [sāman] beginning with *vṛṣāśośiṣṭha*, then *abhiprava*, *śyaita*, *tvāmidā*, *chandasaṃ*, *yasteṣmataṃ*, *pavasvama*, *cchapūṣā*, *suśaṅku*, *sujñāna*, *rīvitāni*, and the single-verse hymns (*ekarccāḥ*). Then follow *pūṣā*, the three-verse hymn, *krauñcaṃ*, *vṛṣā yāmam*, *evāmahī*, *viśvādaṣṭram*, *pūrvamuccā*, *kṣuṣṭambham*, *abhisomadgataṃ*, *aprahinvāṣkārān*, the three *saṃkrośa* verses, *ghatvāṣṭambha*, *bhantaraṇiḥ*, and the three *avanti* verses; this is the third *ṣṭhauha*.

The *asosakhā* verses, the *śaikta*, the two *ekarcas*, the *sutāvanta*, the *tvaṣṭrī*, at the end the *svāsu hiṣṭhīya*, the *varṇaraścyāni*, the *dakṣasākāmantavat*, the eight subsequent [verses], the *abhiṣeṇya*, the *svarpṛṣṭha*, the *punānaḥ*, the *trāviśvāḥ*, the *śokamyoḥ*, the *āpṛśni*, the *aurṇottara*, the *svāsu tva hi*, the *hatkamātīṣā*, the *somaḥ puronānadam*, the *vātsapra*, the *somaḥ saindhukṣitam*, and the *agnim vaḥ*—this is the fourth [section].

Chant this beloved *vita* [hymn] belonging to the *Ṛṣi* Śākala; the *uṣṇih*, *mānava*, *anūpa*, *vāma*, and those dedicated to Agni, as well as the *aśvantāni*, the *vyaśuḥ*, the *dupra-prāṇā*, the *vanakrośa*, the *jasa*, the *avitapārtha*, the *aindrāta*, the *sañjaya*, the *aindrāmitra*, the *asāma-hāmitra*, the *aindrāvṛdhīya*, and the *krauñca*—this is the fifth.

In these very [verses], we should cleanse [the Sāmans]: the *Svāra-aiḍa* on the nostrils of the bull; the *Jajit-varuṇasāma* on the cow-pen; the *Utyaha*, *Devya*, *Revantīya*, *Pari-svāva*, and *Vaidanvata* on the third and fourth [days]; the *Dīrghakārṇa* on the *sasutaṃva*; the *Gaurī-madhu* and *Cunnidhana* on the *somā*; likewise, the *Vāṅnidhana* on the *krauñca*; the *Aiḍa* on the *śnauṣṭama*; the *yāpava* on the *agni*; the *gūrda* on the *pravorca*; and the sixth [Sāman] on the son of Vaśa.

The Vṛṣātaniparṇa, the Ēḍakūlīya, the Nipuṇākaṇvatara, the Gauṅgavayāsya, the Svāsu-pravada-abhinidhana, the Vaikhānasa hymns, "That which is of the ram," the Maukṣa, the Plava of Śarkara, the Sakhā, the Purīvitaka, the Kārttejya, the Kṣāhaviṣa, "He who is old," the Vātsamāta, "Thou art ours," the Sauśravasa, and "If the Vīṅka, O Adhvaryu," in its form—the seventh.

In these very [sections] are: the *aśubhārgī*, *mitraṭatasākalambāni*, *abhisodvihiṅkapārśvahanmagatahārācchidrāṇi*, *prahinvādukthamudvaddhartāyadinaipātithasubhayaṃ vaiyaśvaṃ yuṣaksurūpādyabhāsakākṣīvatāsitānyaṣṭamaḥ*, *dyumnamaiṣiraṃ prāṇātraitamabhīnovitakautsaśuddhākrauñcarayiṣṭhaudalānisvāsudharmahinvaśīya svāsuśanasāṃvarttamārutānijighrataityadārasurūpottarahariśrīnidhanasaindhubābhraveḍānā saṃkṣāraṛṣabhāḥ*—this is the ninth [section].

The *toyi*, the *pṛṣṭhakaulma*, the *puṣpada*, the *dairghatamas*, the *vaiśvadeva*, the *ādyābhīśava*, the *niśrīṇantah*, the *vāsiṣṭha*, the *amasa*, the *sāmarāja*, the *svāsuśrāyantīya*, the *yataḥsamanta*, the *tvasoma*, the *aśvasūkta*, the *śāmmada*, the *avacīna*, the *iḍaviṣkṛta*, the *tvamparṇa*, the *pavasvamanasaṃ*, the *parityaṃvitani*, the *havhiṣṭhīya*, and the tenth.

In these very [days], there are the *asita-sādhra-pārāṇi*, the *svāsu-vidharma-upoṣuḥ*, the *svāsu-aidhmavāhaka-kubhoḥ* and the *dvaśīyāni*, the *uccaiḥ-jigābhi-ke*, the *punar-utsedha-jñīya-niṣedhāni*, the *ājā-vitam-mā-citti-tham*, the *ud-uti-iva-rtta uccha-kulīyam*, the *paryūṣu-śyāvā-gave-dhanva-haviṣam*, the *vāṅ-nidhanam*, the eleven [stotras] of *sūryasya*, the *agniṃ-vāja-jit*, and the *daivya-daśarātra*.

The bull, the purifier of the great earth, the spring, the swimmer, the ancient one—your water flows for the sake of the long-lasting and the powerful. O you who possess clear knowledge, the *krauñca* bird has proclaimed Agni before you; the Soma flows through the months like a horse, the Soma flows as a thunderbolt, moving well toward the good. O you who shine with knowledge, the impelled one is born alone; the all-encompassing one, the son of Rudra, being pressed, is the first among the virtuous.

The *vṛṣāṣmataya* is joined with the subsequent [verse]; the *toṣiñcha* is for the sake of the *ṛc*; the *iḍāmāyāsya* is for the *tṛca*; those desiring prosperity [use] the *triṇidhana*; the *vṛṣāśo* is for the sake of the goal; the *abhipravarta* is for the *śaṅku*; "Purify yourself" (*pavasva*) is for this purpose; the *bhrāma* is for *pūṣan*; the *mahī* is for all; the *daṣṭra* is the subsequent; the *uccā rūpam* is for *abhi*; the *sīravaṃ* is for *pra*; the *hinva* is for *āgneya*; "Come to you" (*ā tvā vartaḥ*) is for *svāsu*; the *kṣullakavāc* is for *sakha*; the *jñānadāsa* is for the sons; the second is for *dhī*.

Pavirājam, pavasva, adāḥ, toṣim, pṛśni, ekasyām, tṛce, bhīśavaḥ, uttare, audhāśrīṇam, uhuve, asya, siṣṭham, yorāvartaḥ, svām, aurṇādi, asujñāne, purastvāṣṭry, ūrdheḍasvāsu, lośādyaiḍa, śuddhīye, arṣā, santani, abhisomān, āvān, upavāmrāni, abhitisampāya, śāvartaḥ, sāgauṣūktam, prāṇājñāne—this is the third [section].

In these very [verses]: *dāsaṃ pavasva*, *avārayiṣṭha*, *masāl uttaraṃ yajiṣṭha*, *sādhyam indrāśva-sūktam*, *mṛjyata tantriṇidhanāya asye sākasiṣṭha*, *piba vartaḥ pari svā idhmavāhantam varcijñānakāśī te svāsuḥ*, *uta āndhena prasorci vartta utsaḥ pratnam varttaleyetathābhi somat saparidhīn duha*—this is the fourth [section]. *Hā u niṣṭram prati lauśādyaṃ mandadugdhā varttaleyet induḥ sampā pavasva tvaṣṭrī dvir abhyastam govil lauśottaram pavam āvṛṣo varttaleyet*.

The *Yāpavāsiṣṭha* is the light of the Maruts; the *Uccāsatra* is the turning back for the sake of Vāyu; the *Puromadhu* is the *Bṛhat* addressed to Agni; the *Abhisoga* is the *Auṅgava*; the *Prahinvān* is the *Audhāsva*;

the *Ādiksusṭambha* is the fifth; the *Ājātama* is the *Aiḍa*; the *Ka-vantaḥ* is the *Pi-manta*; the *Asitam* is the *Vṛṣāyamaiḍa*; the *Ghatvāvarta* consists of three [verses]; the *Sahatvāṣṭrya* is the *Satrātava*; the *Utsedha* is the *Duha*; the *Pṛśni* is the *Śiśu*; the *Pārtha* is the *Dyumna*; the *Prāṇā* is the *Sapha*; the *Śrudhi* consists of single verses; the *Induniṣedha* is the *Dhartṛ*; the *Kāva* is the *Kratustambhasakha*; the *Pauṣkala* is the *Kratu*; the *Śyaita* is the *Pa-ccha*; the *Śrudhi* is the sixth.

The one who possesses the *kratu* flows forth as the *pauṣkala*; this great hymn is for the sake of the *ṛc*. The *sāman* is for the purpose of the goal; he purifies what is placed within. Truly, he flows around the divine Indu, when he has run around the chariot-pole of the sun. He purifies the *paurumīḍha*, the joyous, the new song, the *paridhi*, and the *traiṣṭubha*. He purifies the spring of victory, the most excellent, or him whom they call "this one. These are the single-verse hymns: the *gavaśuddhīya*, the *kratummīḍha*, the *varciśrudhya* as the seventh, the *kratummānava*, the *prāṇa*, the *pauṣkala-kratu*, the *janitra*, the *soma-śrudhya*, the *kratu-dvāja*, the *abhiso'titha*, the *toṣiduktha*, and that which is yours, O Soma—Soma, the *adhyardha*, the *iḍa*, the undeceived.

The *Sumāṇḍava*, the *Asyaja*, the *Ratoṣirava*, the invocation of the gods (*devāniha-vaḥ*), the year (*saṃvatsaraḥ*), the *Pratinānadamāna*, the *Viśvāścaitam*, the *Purodala*, the *Svādoḥśyaitam*, the *Pavasveḍānām*, the *Karcaḥ*, the *Vratnayaudhā*, the *Śiśu*, the divine (*daivyaṅkayā*), the *Svāram*, the *Paripradhanva*, the *Sapham*, the *Ekasyāmuccā*, the *Spāra*, the *Suparṇa*, the *Śākvara*, the *Punāṣṭambhaleya*, the *Śrāyabharanta*, the *Avarovāram*, the *Ekasyāmpurastṛce*, the *Yāsyamaiḍa*, the *Svānojarāvarṇṇa*, the *Iṣam*, the *Punāvaṣaṭkarce*— these are the first [stotriyas].

In the *tṛca* [of the hymn] beginning with "macchaupagavan," there is a prohibition; [the verses] "śrāyamayāpārśvam" and "indrāmahīkarccāḥ" [are used]; in the *tṛca* beginning with "pavasvamaleyaṃ," [there is the verse] "veso yaudhādairgheghādyautānam"; in the *tṛca* beginning with "indumārutasvādijaśānadavaśrudhyandevodarśijñīyam," [there is the verse] "uttemahīmandrajarāpāhiraṃvat"; in the *ṛc* beginning with "karcedairghaṃ," [there is the verse] "viśvasmātsamantantāsvevajayamina auśane," which is the second [verse].

The *kāyat* [is recited] for Agni; the *āyāhi* for the Āghas; the *sam chalayamada* for the Sahitas; the *bhadro no* for the Vājas; the *saphaklekarccau* for the *Tṛca*; the *śrudhi* for the Viśvas; the *vāśvam* for the Ṛc; the *ṛcendhīgavajñīye* for the Samiddha; the *bhīye* for the Kāvas; the *upa tvā vāram ucceṣan* for the *Tokas*; the *jarāsvāsu vaṣaṭ prasotṛ* for the *Gauṅgavas*; the *śagdhi ūhāra* for the *Tvaṅkaulmalas*; the *śumadacyutaḥ* for the Karca; the third [is for the] *Tṛtīya*.

*Pradhvasatram aprasuvan aśvam*—Karkya Audala [is the seer] for the triplet; *pradaijñīya svāsudaiḥ*—Ghaśaghi Ūrvataḥ [is the seer]; *svādiṣkṛtam asya ṣmatam yaḥ te hitam ayam pūrvāśvam*—Vipaścit Bhārgava [is the seer]; *svā suyukta srucam prasunvān*—Gautama [is the seer] for the triplet; *vṛṣājigaḥ svāra-parṇe punādairghyam*—[the seer is] for *yaḥ te surūpa-uttaram tvahi śaṅku su-jñā pavasva deva āsitam ayam pūṣā iti* (this is the fourth).

Uccarṣabha, Śūktābhiṣoma, Utsedha, Svāna, Vāra, Prāṇa, Āśrudhya, Puroniṣedha, Pradhanva, Vapaya, Jighna, Mahīsāka, Pārtha, Imāstvā, Śyaita, Yasya, Leia, Pavamāna, Sahita, Māsa, Gomanna, Sapha, Āśrudhya, Abhīnu, Vāśyā, Vāgave, Jñate, Kāvanta, Oṣi, Daṣṭra, Uttara, Abhitvā, Kaṇva, Ramāṇa, Do, Viśīya; the fifth is Paritya, Śyāvāgave, Pavitra, Kāva, Svādi, Maukṣa, Jñīya, Ṛkṣu, Viśīya, Tvanna, Civāra, Uccāsvāra, Saindhukṣita, Torṣi, Varuṇasāma, Yaḥ, Te, Kākṣya, Chādasa, Puro.
Vādhryava, Etaśa, Havyasātama, Sāman, Trāsada, Agni, Tvashtar, Abhisāvi, Śīya, Svāvāra, Pratūrti, Vartatram, Ṛṣabha, Toṣya, Utsedha—this is the sixth [chapter].
In Utsedha alone are the Śrīṇam, Accha, Śīya, Ayaṃpū, Niṣedha, Indupuṣpa, Cyāvana, and Ekasyām. Pavasva taṃ vaḥ, Purojanitrī, Punāti thaṃ taṃ vaḥ, Śuddhāpadānta.

The *Svādinam*, *Gauḥ-sūkta*, *Aśva-sūkta*, the two single-verse hymns (*ekarcas*), the *Yajñaihi*, *Aṣuta*, *In te*, and *Śrudhi*—these four; then *Piba*, *Utsa*, *Niṣedha*, *Ūṣya*, *Āparṇṇam*, *Aiḍanduhāsam*, and the entire *Paṅkti* hymn; furthermore, the seventh [verse] in the *Varuṇa-sāman*;
*Tavāham*, *Manta*, *Jayera*, *Revatīḥ*, *Devīḥ*, *Svāsu*, *Satrābharantavatī*, and the *Jagatī* verse beginning with *At*.

*soma-sāma-aya-dabhi-tyam-it-pratna-mahīndram-parṇṇamaiḍam-vasu-rucaḥ-satrā-dhayado-viśīyam-pratnam-utsedhas-tad-idośyai-ta-rakṣaḥ-surūpottara-sumanmā-vāram-punāvai-yaśvaṅ-karcovaṣaḍantam-utso-yaste-satrāpavasva-kācīneḍamekāhāḥ*—
thus ends the first chapter.

Panyaṅka, kṣamātva, vidaṣṭraṃ, pūrvaṃ, parisvāsu, rūpottara, svāsu, haviṣ, jarāmārgīya, vāṇī, idaṃ, vām, pavasva, sākam, ṛci, abhisotavo, janitra, iccha, jarāprasos, jarā, somasāma, rohitakūlīyāni, prasokṣārāntaṃ, jayam, uddve, svāraṃ, parṇṇam, acchākṣāram, abhipri, khānasam, asya, pratnāśu, mārgīyave; [this is] the first.

These [hymns] are: *mitraṭata*, *sakalambāni*, *abhisodaḥ*, *dīrghapādvihinkāra*, *daivyam*, likewise *tanihnmeṣu*, *tvāpārśvam*, *asvāsantaniyaste*, *surūpādyabhāsāsitāni*, *abhidyu*, *vācasakhātṛceśauktam*, *indrāsitakautsa*, *śuddhākrauñca*, and *rayiṣṭhāni*; this is the second [section].

The *Indrāpavijñeya*, the *Svasu*, the *Viśīya*, the *Uccāsurūpa*, the *Uttarādāra*, the *Saṃkṣāra*, the *Stoṣi*, the *Pṛśni*, likewise the *Śrīṇasvāna*, the *Hāviṣman*, the *Madāvacīna*, the *Iḍaviṣkṛta*, the *Ayaṃpūjñīya*, the *Hiṣṭīya*, the *Dhartājñīya*, the *Prasupārama*, the *Ayaṃpūkrauñca*, the *Aṅkuṣṭa*, the *Devyantistra*, and the *Aindukṣita*—this is the third [section].

*Sutā tvāṣṭrī*, *svāre punāpṛśni*, *abhīśava uttare*, *siṣṭham ayame devya*, *svāno gauṣūktaṃ prāṇāvāraṃ dasā satrā pari*, *pridvājaṃ ūrmiṇā krośantotopi vāmram ānavānūpāni*, *śrīṇāgneya-somāḥ śyāvāgavaniṣedhāḥ pavasva śyāvāgave*, the fourth [section];

in these very [verses] are the *ākūpāra-soma*s, beginning with *krauñca*, *sunātvāṣṭrī*, *ūrdhveḍapuraḥ*, *śuddhāpadāntam asākṣitam*, *aiḍantaḥ*, *toṣiyaudhāt vaigate śrīhanman*, *puraḥ pāra sādhre pavasva vātreyaṃ pari-pri*.

The *Ṣūktam* (Hymn) in one verse: *pratyasmai vitam indra acyutam prasudānottaram*. In the *Ṛc*: *abhiprijñīyan namaste jarāvṛṣā jñīyasvāsubharam*. In the *Enāmitre*: the fifth [verse], *pavasvadatvāṣṭrīpadīṅkhayantyām abhisodaṣṭrottaram*. In the *Ṛcitṛca*: *abhīśavottara-svaḥ-pṛṣṭha*. *Hinvāvaya me siṣṭham puraḥ kṣullale yan tvam indra dvihiṅkā devyam prāṇāvārśam*. *Pavasva jñīyam bṛhad āgneyan narastodaḥ śrīṇam pibāpṛṣṭham adhvaryo parṇṇaiḍakūlīye*. *Tava hanma gatagauṅgavayāsyāti-tāsudhārā havāśeḥ*. The sixth [section].

Flow on, O Soma, most highly regarded by the seers; flow for Iḍa, Aṅga, and Manu; flow forward for Trita. [The hymns are: the Krauñca for Gautama, the Prosārathi for Traigarta, the Hāuhuva for Viśiṣṭha, the Paritya for Ūrdhva, the Tvāṣṭra for Jñīya, the Punāman for Gakaṇva, the Bhīna for Niṣedha, the Sādhrīya for Nistoma, the Mantu for Punaḥsoma, the Sāmātreyī for Puraḥśiśu, the Hāuhuva for Ayiṣiṣṭha, the Kautsa for Abhīna, the Svāra for Dhartṛ, and the Śārṅga for the seventh.
The Hāuhuva for Akra, the Viśiṣṭha for Pariya, the Asitotara for Indrapāra, the Abhyastan for Karcāvasāya, the Āsama for Aiḍa, the Ājāgṛśana for Paripradhanva, and the Vājaji for Ahīna.

The *viśovit*, *amṛcita*, *vastu*, *ṛca*, *śrudhya*, *yajjiṣṭha*, *aidmajighna*, *parṇaiḍakūlīya*, *santanin*, *punādu*, *uktha*, *pavamāna*, *jarāśravasa*, *abhīnaḥ*, *kārtra*, *pra soma*, *argī*, *pra soma*, *de gata*, *han mahārāyaṇāni*, *svādikākṣībhāsa*, *pra suśuddhā*, *padānta*, *vṛṣāsurūpottara*, and *ṛṣabhe punāpṛṣṭhe* are the first [sections].

In these very [sāmans], there are the Kaulmala, Aiṣa, Śaṅku, Kāṇva, Bhāṣkṛta, Abhiśava, Punarāvarta, Āśva, Auśanasa, Kāma, Idhma-saṅga, Gautama, Pauṣkala, both [the Vāśa and the Anta], Vāśantya, Mānava, Uttaraṅka, Īṅkāṇva, Bhāṣkṛta, Abhiśagdhi, Mānava, Ādya, Mātvā, Vāja, Yaura, Nitra, Yaśas, Tvam, Indrāgni, Mūsa, Trā, Piba, Vāja, Avartta, Kāṇva, Mandra, Abhinidhana, Yathānanā, Anyat, Svamaṅga, and the second [is] the Īḍe.

*Ā tv indra*, *sutodvaśīyam*, *pratiṣyaiṣo jarāśrudhyam*, *uṣastāśvin pratujyotiṣam*, *yat pragāyaty avo idam ābhāḥ*—these are the *auśana* verses; *āśūccātva satrāśrudhyam pavasvābhiprasiṣṭham*, *yadeṣa prakośaḥ*—these belong to the people (*janasyaitāvaḥ*).
*Kāvān itoṣiṅ kaṇvarantante*, *mabharam punāc chandasaṃ ekasyām*, *tṛtīyas tavāhaṃ pṛśni*.
*Ekasyām apsāmārgī gomān āgneyam paṅktyā santanim*, *indro goṣṭhaḥ punā paṅktyāntam*. *Tvāmārgī vayaṅ ghasantani prahinvāc chidram abhīnaḥ*, *tvāṣṭry ekasyām*.
*Tryanta*, *hinva*, *iḍānām*, *upocīna iḍam utsaḥ*, *vitaṅgaviḥ*, *jñīyam*, *pavamākaṇvam*,
*pra soma abhīka-parṇaiḍe*, *pra sodhi hiṅkā devyasvādi-śavam*, *pra su vaiśvāmitra-svāra-kautse*— this is the fourth [section].

In these very [verses] are *aurukṣayam*, *vṛṣā hari-śrīyaḥ*, *te śāmmada-vāśva-sūktāni*, *ayam pūḥ kautsaiḍam uccāmitra-tatasākalambāny-auśana-vairūpa-itisrasuta-sādhravāśvetavāham*, *puṣpada-duktham āṇḍavāni*, *vidāvasv iti yasya nidhanam*, *paripriyām ārgīyavamī-nidhanam puraḥ*.

This is the *śuddhi* [section]. First, the *aiḍa-muṣvāvaiṣṇava*; second, the *uṣvāvaiṣṇava* on a single verse; the *sruccamasā-soma-sāma* on three verses; the *adhyardha-iḍa*; the *pavasva-lāsadasyava*; the *paritya-vāṅnidhana*; the *krauñca* with the *paryūvita* [refrain];

the *ṛcyoka-uṣṇiha*; the *ajīmṛjya-kaṇvara* on a single verse; the *puṣpottara* on three verses; the *vṛṣāṣūkta-kala*; the *punar-bhayataḥ-stobha-gautama*; the *purastvāṣṭrī* ending in *svāra* and ending in *ā*; the *uccāmārgī*; the *punādvi-hiṅkāra-devyagata-puṣpa*; the *ayann-pū*; the *madhuścut*; the *ojipuṣpottara*; sixth, the *svādyāśva-sūkta* on a single verse; and the *satrāṇi*.

*Pratnam-udvat*, *upaśikṣāsapha*, *indra*, *viśvāla*, *iyantam-vobharantu*, *amaṅga-kakubham*, *varivaḥ-sāhīyam*, *utsaḥ-abhinidhanam*, *kāṇvam-eṣa-brahma-āleyam*, *āṣkṛtam-tam-vaḥ-vayam*, *utvā-āleyam*, *upa-davi-pavajñīyāni*, *suśikṣāsapha-ṣkala*, *ṛkṣau-matsya-āleyam*, *tṛce-svāmu-dhasam*, *uttarayoḥ-kakub-ātvā-āleyam*, *paripradhanva-pauṣkalam*, *ekasyām-svādi-kautsam*, *aiḍe-prathamaḥ*.

*sakhākrauñcam*, *mayampūṣā*, *iti yadvitīyam evābharat*, *indram viśvā medhaṃ*, *indrāyāhi dhiye gāyanti te*, *ayam āyaḥ puraṃ na magne takam*, *aśvam enā pratyu imā uvāma*, and *iti ca*—in each of these [verses], one should recite the *devyaśrudhyāni* at the juncture (*sandhau*) with *agne vivasva*. These are for the *yajñāmahā vaiśvāmitre* (the second [section]). In these very [verses] are the *dairghamacikrahitam*, the *pavasva vaṣaṭkarcaḥ*, the *purojñīyam*, and [the verses] following the *gāyatrī*: *vidhuṃ*, *vaṣaṭvaṇ*, *kim it te viti*, *śrāyantīyam*, *pavasvāndhī*, and *pavasva soma utsa dyotānam*. These are the expiations (*prāyaścittāni*) consisting of single-verse hymns (*ekarcāḥ*).

*Abhitvā*, *Kaṇva-ranuttara*, *Eka-kubha*, *Indu*, *Naudhasa*, *Śyaita*, *Sana*, *Kautsa*, *Aiḍa*, *Utsa*, *Dhasu*, *Purastṛca*, *Pāra*, *Abhyasta*, *Yat-puru-utsa*, *Śyaita-purodhasa*, *Karccāsta*, *Vodhasa*, *Naudhasa*, *Śyaita*, *Abhipravaḥ*, *Śyaita-naudhasa*, *Abhitvā-tvām-it*, *Hivāretam-vodā*, *Abhipravaḥ*, *Krauñca*, *Abhitvā-pūrva*, *Kaṇvaraṃ-tvāmi-tvahi-ehi-kaṇva*, *Bṛhat*, *Yad-yāya-dimat*, *Mahā-vaiṣṭambha*: the first [is thus].

"Drink, hear us"—in these [verses] beginning with *pibā śrudhi*, there are four; "to Indra, the giver of wealth"—in these [verses] beginning with *evam arāya revāt*, there are six; "the pressed juices, most excellent"—in these [verses] beginning with *pra so prasū kaṇvataram*, there are three; "Pūṣan for Kaṇva, the great"—in these [verses] beginning with *abhi sosutaḥ*, there are two; "O Indra, this [Soma] is dear to you"—in these [verses] beginning with *aṣṭamaṃ te vapus*, there are two; "O Indu, this gift for Indra"—in these [verses] beginning with *imam āsitam asā tvāṣṭrī*, there are two; "when Indra shattered the cities"—in these [verses] beginning with *yat indra vipriyam purām bhinduḥ*, there are two; "the second [verse] belongs to Viśvāmitra"; "they sing to you repeatedly"—in these [verses] beginning with *sābhyāsam tvāṣṭryā*, there are two; "Indra by means of the Krauñca"—in these [verses] beginning with *indrayākrauñca*, there are two; "this [Soma] has been drunk"—in these [verses] beginning with *imam asāgāyama indrayā*, there are two; "the god who protects"—in these [verses] beginning with *avitāni devaḥ*, there are two.

The *Kaṇvaravañjña*, the *Kaṇvabṛhat*, the *Purovāt*, the *Prajanitājñīya*, the *Svāsu*, the *Marāyan*, the *Tvaṃdyāśu*, the *Dhāsuṣvāpāraṅkarccausomaḥ*, the *Pavanta-jñīya*, the *Svāsuvārāghajanitāśyāvāśvam*, the *Prateśaikhaṇḍinam*, the *Govicchyenaḥ*, the *Tantvāhavaddevyara-saṃmārgīyave*— this is the third [section].

With the *ayāpavā* [verse], he quickens the light; with the *jāgata*, the *varuṇasāman*; with the *pravat*, he raises the *śiśu*; with the *sāmarāja*, he impels the *śiśu*; he steps upon the light; with the *vātsapra*, he steps upon the light; with the *śṛṅga*, he impels the *ājā*; with the *punāyāma*, he impels the *gorāṅgirasa*; with the *somīya*, he impels this *utya*; with the *prova*, the boar; with the *uhuvāyi*, the sustainer; with the *uhuvāsa*, the most excellent; with the *proāmīva*, the sustainer; with the *krande*, the *sāvi*; with the *siṣmān*, the fourth [is concluded].
"pra vājī bodhi," "iyad-darśyam," "abhinidhanam kāṇvam agne," "āindram manaḥ," "naipātitham," "āccha śrāyantīyam," "kṣudrāḥ śrāyantīyam"—these are the Bṛhat-stotriyas.
Thus ends the section on the Bṛhat-stotriyas.

Most easily to be won, unassailable, you have been invoked; with this great [Soma], flow through the intermediate space. Flow as the *vairūpa* purifier, uninjured, as the *ātharvaṇa*. Drink, O Great One, as the *vairāja*; flow for the sake of the sacrifice, O Indu. Thus Indra [drank] the great [draught]. O ray of light, flow as the sweet, vigorous one; flow for the bull, the *iḍā*, for Indra, O Indu, as the wealthy ones, the well-formed bull, for the sake of the *bhaya* and the *śyena*. This is auspicious for me. That which is your hymn (*arka*), flow as the lord of the regions; your hymn praises the established places, the splendors, and the glories. The best presser is the hymn; who is the protector? The ten-night rite.

*Punānaṃ*, *abhi somāḥ*, *ruśantam*, *vaṇan*, *marṣā*, *apatyaśākvare*, *yajñāyajñā ca*, *taraṃ matsi*, *bṛhat praty asmai*, *taraṃ yajñā*, *prasusvaraṃ caturthaṃ matsi*, *yaṃ pūṣā*, *dvitīyam etāsv eva*, *tṛtīyaṃ praty asmai sutāsaḥ*, *prathamasya pratnām*, *bhrāja vibhrāṭ tava vaṇ*, *indram id śrāyantaḥ*, *kīrtyam indra kratu-puraḥ*.

Śrāyavikarṇa, parisvāna, ābhrāja, uccāgneḥ, vratam, mūrdhā, purobhās, tava, ahaṃ, antaram, puraḥ, jibṛhat, parītaḥ, tarat, revatīḥ, revatyaḥ, tvam, agne, bṛhat, abhi, saḥ, pari, itaḥ, vāk, karambhāt, yotaret, tat, id, ātri, karājan, devyāḥ, parisvānaḥ, svāśiraḥ, markaḥ, agne, tava, ṣaṭ, ṛce, lāndasam, saṃvatsaraḥ.

The *purojava* [is] *vaṇasvādin*; the *śiras* [is] *marka*; the *arka* [is] *uṣṇihā*; the *yaste* [is] *vārṣāhara*; having pierced through [them], you are the *uttara*; the *bṛhat* [is] *dvipadottara*; the *paryūṣan* [is] *nada*; the *stobha* [is] *punāna*; the *saptaha* [is] *mekasyām*; the *dhartṛ* [is] *dīrghatamas*; the *arka* [is] *yaḥ pūrbhagaḥ svāsu*; the *sāman* [is] *abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ*; the *bṛhat* [is] *ye te svāśiraḥ markaḥ*; the *kimīdin* [is] *bṛhat pavate yaḥ te balabhide*; the *ekarcā* [is] *tvam indra yaśāḥ*; the *purojit* [is] *bhargaḥ*; the *punāna* [is] *sthāna*; the *svāsu* [is] *saptaha*; the two *sāmans* [are] *halye*; the *pura* [is] *indu*; the *ekarca* [is] *ekāhāḥ*.

The Ājyadoha hymns, the *pratiloma* (reversed) verses, "pra sunvānaḥ," "tisro vācaḥ," the *śrāyakṛti*, the *svāsuśma*, the *aśvavrata*, the *abhivājī*, the *vyāhṛtisāman*s, the five [verses] beginning with "bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ," "satyam puruṣaḥ," the *svarṇidhana*, the *pūtamasa* hymn, the *karca*s, the three [verses] beginning with "śrīṇā sthāna," the *arka* of Agni, "paripradhanva," the *dīrghatamas-arka*, "abhitvā vṛṣan bhara," "taraṃ yajjābṛhat," "abhiprivṛṣā pavitradhartā"—these are the *stobha*s; the four *iḍā*s consisting of four, six, eight, and ten [syllables]; and the *arka* "punānaḥ paripriyāḥ" with the *svāśira* mixture. The pressed [juice] is the *marka*.

The *Bṛhat* [Sāman] has the Puroruc; "O Jambha," etc., ends with Soma; the intermediate space is toward the golden Agni; "Vājīya" is for Agni; the *arka* of Dīrghatamas is twice; the *arka* is all around; those lacking milk; "Do not fear," etc.; Agni, the great one; the *Vājīya* verses are in response; "toward the beloved," etc.; the *arka* of Dīrghatamas; that splendor; the enclosures; Atharvan; mixing; from the darkness; all around; the single-verse hymns; for purification; fame; "O Jambha," etc.; the upper spring; the serpent; the highest; having proclaimed; "toward the front," etc.; the second; the sacrificial sessions.

To that very forest-slope, the bull and the solitary bull [proceed]; the Aśvins' vow is supreme; in these very vows of the waters, again, the vow of the cows is superior; may we not go against this [vow] hereafter; O Agni Vivasvat, in the Trikadruka vessels, the great [hymn]; O Agni Vivasvat, the ancient friend for the sake of glory; in the Pratiloma [rite], the path for the cow; the expiations.

The *yajñendu* consists of one verse; the *sakhāyodha* consists of two verses; the *bṛhat* consists of three verses; the *paritandu* consists of two verses; one should repeat twice the two-footed [verse]; the *punātara* is the spring (*utsa*); the *pratna* is repeated twice; the *abhitvātaḥ* is the *bṛhat*; the *tvāmibṛhat* is the *taraṇi*; the *tvāmihā* is the *jambha*; the *svāsu* is short; the *yadindra* is the *iti ca*; the *yadyā* is the *yadindra*; the *vāntarikṣe* is the *svāsu*; the *ṣabhaḥ* is the *śrudhī havam*; the *iti ca* is the *trikapra*; the *uṣuvatsa* is the *atīṣaṅga*; the *yadindra* is the *indrāya āhi*; the *pūnāpūṣa* is the *jambha*; the *adyamabhi* is the *so hrasvāsu*; the *tāsaḥ* is short; the *antarikṣe* is the *tava purā*; the *iti vairāja* is the *ṛṣabha*; the *soma* is the *oṣva*; the *pavasva* is the *vatsa*; the *tayoreva* is the *atīṣaṅga*.

*Prasūḥ prasūtaraṃ punaḥ pūṣā bṛhad abhi suta aso ruper tavapuḥ etā mahā vairājaṃ pari svārevatyo abhi so suta tarantaṃ va bṛhat soma uṣvā pavasva taraṃ mṛjya soma abṛhat pavasva śreyaḥ suta asi iṣṭam agna ā yāhi antarikṣa hotāraṃ vatsā akran tamasaḥ soma uṣvā pavasva simāḥ kṣudrā iti kṣudrā iti.* Thus ends the section on the *laghu-stotriyas*.
This is the second *prapāṭhaka*.

That which is palatal and augmented becomes *āyi*; that which is not augmented remains as it is by its original nature (*prakṛti*). These [cases] where *āyi* is obtained become *oyi*. Indeed, in the *saubhara*, *āmahīyava*, and *ehīmi* sections, it is *ahi*; however, in the *daivodāsa* section, it is *ahikaulma*, and the vowel *e* which is obtained by its original nature becomes *ai*. Furthermore, in the *daivodāsa* section, even that which is not augmented becomes *āyi*. In the *tāva* section of the *pavate* [hymn], in the *krauñca* [sāman], and in the *vasonireka* *abhinidhana*, that which is augmented remains as its original nature (*prakṛti*). Its inclusion [in the rule] is for the sake of the *nidhana* [verse]: "hīṣīstha. Everywhere, it is not *jina*.

O bull, [you struck] the infant at night; the ancient one, with praises, [you] made to flow. O Soma, you conquered these [powers] by your wondrous deeds; you shattered the mountain for the sake of the Maruts. O Indra, do not abandon us; protect us in the battle against the Dāsas. O you who extend the lineage, [protect] us in the conflict.

May the Soma-drop, the seer, sit within the dwelling of the warrior-god; by whom, O Goddess, you bestow threefold nourishment for the sake of prosperity. He has entered his own place in the vat; he has stepped upon the pressed juices everywhere. Indra, the winner of waters, is present everywhere; he who is self-ruling, pure, and ageless is to be known in the *bodhīya* verses. In the *vājinejiti*, *snathī*, and *ghajī* [verses], he who is increased from the ancient source is everywhere to be proclaimed. May there be no affliction or obstruction for him; may the Soma-hymns be effective. In the *śvāghī*, *dhīgaca*, and *vajina* praises, he has attained the third station. In the third [station], he has gladdened the one to be known; he has bestowed gifts everywhere.
In which [verses] the *nārmema*, *dabhiḥ*, *vyābhiḥ*, *tiśṛ*, *hmāṇikā*, and *kāṇve* proceed;

in the *prathamaḥ kakṣe-sute*, in the *rātridāseṣi*, in the *rātripāre-kūrmimārṣabhe-mākīm-gāre-bhayin-nani-gobhiḥ*; in this *saumedheta-ye-huvani-dhanayoḥ*, in the *kautseṣu*, in the *mani-yaudhādeva-sapheṣi*, in the *aiḍayāsyepasi-dasi-nodgīthāda-yaḥ*, [these are] the second.

You go to the earth, you go to the *ṣiṣṭha* (the most excellent), you go to the *śyaita* melodies; they enter the *chandasa* meters. Truly, they go with the ancient stations. We have fashioned a great *śakuti* (a ritual act) with the *krauñca* chants. In the first [station], the two fangs are set against the Lord. I take hold of the second, supporting it. Everywhere, name and form are found in the *mitravilamba* (friend-stopping) movements, in the *madgemanī* (gliding) and the *saṃkrośa* (shouting). The bearer (*vahni*) is in the *tiṃvramanī* (swift-moving) state. In the exhilaration of the *dhena* (milk-cow), he stands firm in the support (*ṣṭambhe*). He stands at the sound (*rave*), he stands at the *ṣṭhauhī* (the four-year-old cow). The third [station] is that which goes forth.

For the sake of the splendor of Śaukti, for Tvaṣṭṛ’s own possession, for the sake of the vigilant ones—be resplendent with your powers! O you of golden hue, you have conquered the wives; you are the archer, the provider, the nourisher, the one who strikes the foe. You are the winner of wealth, the one who prevails over the enemy, the steadfast one in the midst of the trembling host. When the speckled one has run forth, the woolly one has gone toward the sacrifice; the great one has been brought as a gift, the one who carries the oblation. O Agni, the distant one approaches you, the son of Sindhu-kṣit, the fourth [priest].

*Priyaidrā*, *jyeṣṭhaṃ harī*, *bravītsu indra*, *viteheśa dhryaśvatṛbhiḥ*, *yeva pego vāmremandī*, *yānidhyaśvetānyagneḥ*, *triṇidhanemandī*, *ca śeśayūṣipatīpūrvaṃ*, *nāpi vaneśyatiḥ*, *krośepriyā*, *trīṇi te sarvatra vivṛttam*, *aṅkārapratyayaṃ na marmṛjyante*, *hitepavatedāśaspatye*, *pārthejabhrasarvatra dāśaspatyerāti*, *sakhī sañjayedyavi mitrekṛvṛta cite syave asipūrvaṃ*, *mahāmitregahi harī*, *krauñce cauvi sarvatra pañamaḥ*.

In *rayiraṃdha*, *nvasirayu*, *ruṇasāmnī*, and *bhirvantīya*, all [verses] have the *asinidhana* ending. In the first *paritrēsa*, it is everywhere *tuve saḥ pī*. In the second, *kaviḥ tuve śve saḥ pī*. In the third, *dīrghaindraḥ āye namikārṇaśravasāiva vitere sarvatra kroñcedhīyāḥ śrauṣṭe sūni jūnti sūni gūrde ṣṭhadī*;
this is the sixth.

Among the Taniparṇa and Kulīya clans, you indeed seek out those others; you go first, you are a giver, you are dear, you are a helper. For you, the pressed juice is for the one who is alone; you manifest yourself to Kaṇva, O self-resounding one, at the dwelling of Khānasi. At the approach of the sacrifice, you release us with your protections; you are the armor for the singer, the refuge for the one who approaches. You are the youth, the one who brings fame, like a swift steed for the one who exerts himself in the offering. Come to Vātsa, come to Vīṅka; you are the hero for the hero who roars, O Indu, for the sake of purification. You are the seventh among all things, the milk for Indra, for the one who purifies himself; you are the leaf, the side, the slayer of enemies, the one who has reached the mind through hymns, and those who are raised up among the Bhṛgus.
With the men [as steeds], by the new will, he has been praised;

the eighth [verse] was sought. He has shone forth, the second, the ancient one; the lord of heaven, the upholder, you are the sustainer of the people. O Indra, great is your power; you stand firm in the law. You are the sage among the Maruts; you are the one who leads them. You are the protector in the battle; you are the ninth [in the sequence]. O Bhīṣu, when the Soma is pressed, you rule over the assembly; you go toward the one who comes for help, drawn across the river, in the first [stanza].
In the *mantas* [of the *Ṛgveda*], in the *udgītha*, you are the one who shines forth; in the *nihava*, everywhere, you are the tenth;

in the *sita*, everywhere, in the *mada*, in the *nara*, everywhere, in the *vidharman*, they go; in the *traikakuba*, in the *vivāpa*, I am the master; in the *vaśīya*, in the *mīra*, the *śāma* has conquered; in the *tejā*, in the *ābhīka*, it is given; in the *jñīya*, you are the first; the *varttati* is meditated upon; the *rohit* is the first; in the *sāī*, with the horse, I have won; in the *abhidhīga*, in the *pārinā*, for the sake of the great, I have struck; in the *devya*, the ten nights are kindled.
He speaks to Pārtha with that speed; he is mindful with his thoughts and inspired songs. He is not struck down by the one who is more powerful; like great wheels, he does not falter.

Everywhere the suffix *makāra* is applied in the first [verse]. He impels for you, O giver of the oblation; you are the one to be praised. Those [deeds] of Pārtha are in the wheel, in the small [space], in the praise, and in the flow. The great toothed one, the lord, is like a form of splendor, O Agni. With the subduing ones, those who are most excellent among these, they have sacrificed to me. For the sake of the gift, for the sake of the cow, for the sake of the trembling one, the former [is established].

The second [verse]: O King of the Gods, these [sacrificial offerings] flow; they are purified by the pressing-stones. O Bhīṣaja, for you, the son of Uśij, they have been brought together with golden ornaments. They have surrounded the dwelling-place of the ancient Ārṇava. The pure Kavi, who is higher, has purified himself with the glowing wool of the sheep. He, the wise one, has fashioned wealth with horses and bulls.
The voices have come together like waters in their flow. The third [verse]: He has subdued the enemies.

In *dāse*, *trīṇi*, *rayiṣṭhoḥ*, and *maṇipūrvam*; in *dvya* and *bhyām*, [the word] *lośe*; in *rāje*, *sādhye*, and *śreṣṭhe*; in *antevāre*, *siṣṭhe*, and *nutrīḥ*; in *nakṣe*, *dhanve*, *striyāḥ*, *bhiḥ*, *sacate*, *sume*, *ṇanti*, *vartte*, *diye*, *marutām*, *dhenoḥ*, *mani*, *yadi*, *nuṣī*, *vartte*, *deva*, *gṛviḥ*, *sarvatra*, *nājau*, *itajñīyayoḥ*, *janakāve*, *prasotari*, and *ayoḥ*; and in *utsavartte*—in these cases, the fourth syllable is *deva*.

The two sages, O Maruts, are praised with hymns; they go toward the assembly like a prize-winning steed. These [songs] are for you both, in your own essence; may they be established through the best of offerings. O Maruts, the gods have come to the mountain; let the two of you, swift on the chariot, drive the prize toward us. This fifth [hymn] is for the sake of the singer; it is a great song upon the white [soma], a friend in the mind of the singer. The golden-hued one dwells with Kaṇva; he has come to the side of the two sages. May the two of you, O Maruts, be present in the cloud; may you be established everywhere in the firm foundation.
For glory, he is the youngest; he is the sixth in the dwelling-place, the one who dwells in the secure abode.
O Pārthya, come hither; you have joined the two excellent steeds. He has been united with the powerful ones;
for the sake of great Indra, he has been brought from Kāva. From Indra, the light has been cleansed for the bountiful one; this is the seventh [verse].

In the *ṣkale* [chant], in the *triṣṭubh*, in the *haduttha*, in the *sute*, the year (*saṃvatsara*) is praised; in the *īśā*, in the *yauṣmadasī*, in the *sarvatrapūṣā*, in the *canas-tobha*, in the *pratyaya*, in the *yūtha*, in the *svāra*, in the *parṇa*, in the *trīṇām-sapha*,
and in the *indrā-pūṣṇe-bodhīya*, this is the first.

With the ancient songs, O Maruts, you were formerly praised at the drinking and the resting place; for the great battle against the Dasyus, you brought light with your rays. In the first age, you established the heavens; hear our great invocation. He was born from the horse; he knows his own source. He poured forth the stream, the bearer of the oblation, as one who knows. These very things we proclaim in our hymns; they have been seen in hundreds of places.
Through the auspicious and swift steeds, the second [birth] was manifested.

O Goddess Agni, you bestow the flaming sacrificial grass; O Agni, you delight in the hair-like flames established upon the altar. Agni is swift; Agni is like a lowing cow. May he be known as dear in the distance, may he be known as one in the nearness. When you, O Kāvya, are with the twenty-one-fold [sacrifice], they go forth with these toward the offering. For there are no bonds for the one who knows the truth; the third [step] shatters them. May those divine powers turn toward us; may the two worlds be well-disposed to our gift.

In all places, together with those [powers], the beloved ones flow like rivers; the seers have praised the radiant one here. He has gone forth, impelling the white-rayed light; this is the fourth [hymn].

In the sixfold *vaṃtīya*, those which are in the *vāra* [sections], those which are in the *varīṣu*, and those which are established for the sake of ritual action (*kratve*)—these are on the side of the *lepa*. Those which are joined with you, O Jyotis, shine among us; the light, the light, O Sapha-deva, by the seer Kavi.
The light of the mountain, O Indra, is in the *udgītha*; the fifth [verse] belongs to the seer Kavi.
This is the birthplace of Maukṣeya; it is scattered in the *vāja-vantīya*. With the waters in the final *ruṇasāman*, it is poured out in the *dāsya*.

With these [verses] one should proceed; the sixth [verse] is for the root *ṣidh* (to succeed), "May wealth come hither. With the following [verses], "Come hither with the doors," and "Thou art in the doors, O protector," one listens to the invocation. With the verses beginning "O you who are ever-active," and "In the *ruṇasāman* with men," the seventh [section is completed].
In the *Yaudhāparyudgītha*, [it is said]: "O Goddess, come to the water-digging with the waters; O victorious one, that which is yours, the light, by that [light] [come] to these one-day sacrifices.
This is the third chapter.
Now begins the fourth chapter:

*kakṣemāt*, *nāre ūtiḥ*, *svarvat nidhanam*, *pari pūṣṇe mahe peyāt*, *kratve śve ca bodhīya īśaye dhiye mārgīyavā ekine jaye kṣārānte*, *deva vaikhānase priyā prathamaḥ tanith abhi pārśve gahi vācaḥ sāmni dīdvidīyam*. *Deva vahniḥ stāve svarī śaukte śriye site sane made*—this is the second [section].

They strike at what is to be known; he goes toward that which is to be known. He dwells in the beloved, in the place of purification, for those who have attained it. O Sustainer, you are to be known by me, O Goddess, as this beloved third one. Sit with the men for the sake of the fearful one; those things which are on the earth, they remain there. O Goddess, may she be victorious; let her cry out with great splendor through her insights. When the horse is pressed, let the insights seek the cow; let the insights be established in the fourth.
Let the third be known among the gods; let the god be awakened in the third. Let the insight be known; this is the fifth.

The two *iḍā* verses for Tvaṣṭṛ; the *bhīśu* and *vemanī*; the *siṣṭha* and *mathi*; the *gahi*; the *vārṣe*; the *priyā*; the *jñīya* and *cātīsara*; the *navāśva* and *dhīgava*; the *hadāgneya*; the *dūregata*; the *teti*; the *gau* and *gavediva*; the *pūrva*; the *pariyāsi*; the *paryudgītha*; the *divāyāni*; the *pārtha*;
the *tāni*; the *rāhe*; the *vāśe*; the *śīpra*; and the sixth is the *āṣa*.

The charioteer has led [him] as if toward the dawn; he stirs our thoughts like a milch-cow. He, the most excellent one, is to be praised by the three times seven [priests]. Those [deeds] which were performed for Pārtha, those indeed are celebrated in the lineage of Viśvāmitra. He who knows the secret counsel of the two [divinities] is to be praised among men in the dwelling place of the gods.

O Soma-drinker, you are the best of the ancient ones; the tawny-hued one is the seventh in the line of Śārṅga. You are the leader of the Vasiṣṭhas; lead the gods with your power. You go to the light, you go upon this path.

May the wise Śanematī come with aid; may the hero protect us from the lowly ones. With his mind fixed on the goal, he is the first, like a spearman clad in armor. Those [deeds] which were performed by the son of Uśanas, by Skala, by Nemi, by Vāśa, by Mānava, and by Vedhas at the place of the Āṣkāra-dhana—Indra indeed did not withhold them. The glorious deeds of Indra are unique; alone he has turned them toward you within. Come with joyous songs; even those who restrain themselves have gone beyond. O you who are deep in the heart, come to the sacrifice; let there be gifts for the throat.

Speak in the midst of the assembly as the second; be mindful of her who desires to see you, and be mindful of her who desires to hear you here at this Vaiśvajyotis sacrifice. Sit down with that by which one knows the slow-moving and the swift-moving; may she come hither. O God, in the dwelling of the gods, in the chariot-ride of the gods, remember those auspicious songs in the Vaidhṛti meters. These prayers are for Kavi; O Kavi, partake of them in the battle. Bring the wives first; this is the third [offering].

The *agni* [nidhana] has three [verses]; the *mandī* [nidhana] has two; the *saṅkṣāra* [nidhana] has two; the *jñīya* [nidhana] has two; the *sīvītīsā* [nidhana] has two; the *jyotiḥpāvī* [nidhana] has two; the *svāra* [nidhana] has two; the fourth [nidhana] in the *kautsa* [chanting] is the *śrīnidhana*;

in the *kautsa* [chanting] it is the *hinve*; [the verses are]: "He seeks dear wealth" (*priyāḥ rayim eṭate*), "the mindful ones" (*mnāni śane*), "the extenders" (*yarntāḥ*), "in form" (*rūpe*), "the milch-cow" (*dhena*), "the Brahmins" (*brarhmāḥ*), "to the virtuous" (*sādhre*), "to heaven" (*dive*), "first" (*pūrvaṃ*), "in the horse" (*vāśve*), "the two banks" (*tīrā ve pūrvaṃ*), "to Mārgīyu" (*mārgīyave*), and "the great" (*mahī*)—this is the fifth [section].

In the *sruca* chant, in the *krauñca* exhilaration, in the *śākala* and *anuvāka*, in the *nidhana* with the sound *āṣ*, in the *mārgīyava* chant, in the *tejā* and *dvigarta* chants, sit down! In the *satrāṇi*, in the *saphe*, teach us, O finder! In the *traikakubha* chant, speak! In the *gītha*, in the *kāṇva*, in the *rinna*, we have approached you; in the *jñīyeta*, in the *davi-jñīyeta*, in the *hetṛ-kramīt*, in the *pavajñīya*, in the *vāra*, in the *nadha*, in the *saphe*, in the *sunve*, in the *sukṣipkala*, teach us, O finder!
One should take the *rayiṃ* [verse] in the *nasta*; for the *hiśṛ* [verse], the *naudhasa* as previously stated, is to be taken in the *leya* at the *ṣkala*.

Indra is the first in the *bhara*; the *brahme* [verse] in the *nārmedha* is the lord in the fourth tone. One should take the *abhi* [verse] in the *leya*; in the *envī* [verse], one should take the *pare* [verse] in the *leya*. In the *yūthe*, the *ṣṇire* [verse] is for *kamaśvermiṇīn*; in the *mātrī* [verse], it is for *vāre śi stri tavet*. For the divine, it is for *darśi*; for the divine, it is for *code*; for *śrudhye*, it is for the two *śvibhyām*; this is the second.

With the *sahiterī*, with those [hymns] by which the all-effecting one is known, for the sake of the young one, in the *śrāyantīya* [chant], toward the god, the expiations are performed with the *ṇvatara*. O Indra, you bestow upon the young one the *śyaita* and *dhasi*; with the *itṛ*, with the *sreṇi*, with the *nīkera*, in the *krauñca*, in the *bhīpare*, in the *krauñca*, in the *jarī*, in the *hasra*, those [songs] of the singer (*gireḥ*) with the *ṇvatara*s; in the *āsyeṭ*, in the *ṣṭambha*, in the *tāsī*, the first [is] with force (*sahaḥ*), in the *dairgha*, the mountain-like (*śvādriḥ*) one beyond the force, in the *dairgha*, the *nīṣā* accompanies; I speak in the higher [verse], in the *arāya*, in the *nīṣī*, in the *māra*, with the *vāra*s, in the *ṇvatara*, in the *theṣṭambha*, in the *syeśā*, O friend, yours is the joy; for the sake of wealth, around the *vāra*, you enter the *ṇasiṃ*; O Tvaṣṭṛ’s son, come to the two bay horses (*harī*).

The sage, the wielder of the thunderbolt, is there with his great friends, the Siṣṭhapriyas; he is the second among those who are praised with hymns. When the cry of the crane resounds, the wise one has extended himself. O Indra, at the pressing of the juice, the singer has offered praises. The god has looked upon the two worlds; the wise one has known the mortal. He has kindled Agni; once kindled, he shines in the choice vessel. This is the third [verse] of Agni Śaikhaṇḍin, which was sung by the son of Aśva. If the falcon flies toward the deer, this is the third [verse] of Mārgīyava.

In this world, those [hymns] of Vārtrature, Śnauṣṭi, and the descendant of Bhṛgu (Bhārgava) are proclaimed; [the hymn] with the word *tisā* is for the one possessing speed (*jūtimat*), and that which begins with *udvat* is for the descendant of Bhṛgu. With that by which he goes, the seer-made [hymn] is for the King of Sāman; in the first [part], O God, delight yourself. Kutsa, the son of Adhiratha, chooses the light; he comes singing, for the one possessing speed, having stepped forth toward the light in the first [part]. O God, choose the firm [path]; the army of the gods marched forward in the first journey. In the *vic* [verse] addressed to Gaurivīti Āṅgirasa, he stepped toward the cows. In the *asomīya* [hymn] addressed to Indra, it was called out loudly by Siṣṭha. In the kingdom of Indra, the fourth [part] does not fail.
The waters flow swiftly with prayers; the earth trembles before you. O Indra, your two bay steeds are within; you are the lord of the waters that come to you.

The small ones are in the second enclosure, while the third is extended by the master. O Soma-drinker, the filters are unharmed; the three are in the Vairāja hymn, and the three belong to Bṛhadgiras. O Indra, the two bay steeds are in the rays; he is the vigorous one in the juice. In the eighth [verse], the waters are in the *ḍermaṇi* verses; O Indra, the bull is in the Raivata hymn. O Indra, the hawk has long power; the former gods are auspicious with the Rudras at the first turning.
To Bharga, the oblation; to Tama, the King of the Sun; the Seer is in the crossing over the fears. The ten-night sacrifice is for you; may the sacrifice cross over in the great *ṣāta*.

He has turned toward this sacrifice in the resonance; in that resonance, may he impel it. *Sāvī* is the head; *bhāsa* is Agni; *tīṣu* is indeed the great *hiva*. In the grasping, the oblation is for the King; the sweet drink is for the warrior. The self-mixed [drink] is for the Seer of the *arka*; the all-nourishing is for the first *ilānd*. *Mīyā* is for the *ṣibhā*; *ṇākṣī* is for the second; *agneṇākṣī* is for the third. Great is Agni; the stain is for the gods; the year is complete.

O Hari, he who was first in the choice, in the trembling, in the song, in the stream, in the supreme praise, in the threefold darkness, with men, with the sun—He, the golden one, with the waters, with the limbs of the calf, the golden one, with the rays, toward the east, in the lofty hymn, in the light, in the sky, in the former greatness, in this world, in the breaking of the clouds, in the mouth—the *kāhas*.

Those [verses] which are for Pārtha are in the second milking; those which are in the *ptaṃkrośa* are in the third; the excellent ones are in the *aśvavrata*; *śmati* is in the *vasvī*; this one is in the *ayaṃpū*; *patiḥ* is in the *tamasoḥ*; *svarvat* is in the *nidhana*; those which are in the *paripra tamasoḥ* are in the *arka*; *te so ca taredvīṣām* is in the *bṛhat*; *pṛthivīm svāśirām* is in the *arka*; the *kaviḥ śuciḥ* is in the *mahī*; *bṛhati dive pūrvam* is in the *vājī*; *agniṃ payasi* is in the *viśve*; [these are] the *timāhīnāḥ*.

In the first [verse] there is the Vājī; Agni is in the second; in the great third, he has overcome the nights. With his own powers, he has driven away the darkness with rays. Those who come from above, from the darkness, through the sun; in the second [verse], the *parisatrāṇi* (enclosures) in the *sandhi* (junction), in the great *bṛhatī*. O Agni, in your great, swelling, auspicious *triṣṭubh*, you have established the *bṛhat*.

In which watch [of the night] one should proceed; the expiations (*prāyaścittāni*) are indeed in the *Ṛkṣi* and the *Vairājarṣabha*. There is protection in the *Trāṇi*, in the *Hasī*, and in the *Ṣau-ttare-bhe*. I shall speak of the *Nī-ṣī-vāmīt*. Together with the *Vatsā* and the *Proṣuvatsā*; in the *Saṅga*, in the *Atīṣaṅga*, in the *Anvī*, in the *Hrasvā*, in the *Saṃkha*, in the *Vatsā*, and in the *Avī*—just as the *Yega* is in the *Vajravatsā*—and in the *Tre-dhā-vīñca*. These very same [expiations apply] except for the two *Atīṣaṅgīs*.

The *sutā* (pressed juice) is indeed yours in the vast sky, O friend, as it was before; in the unharmed cow-pen, sacrifice to Agni. Having overcome those who are hostile, may you rejoice in the light of the sun. Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, [is present] in the first [verse]; in the second is the fulfillment (*pūrti*); in the third is the *chāndasī*. In the *simākhatī* verses, the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) has been explained by means of the *ṣaṅga*.
Thus ends the fourth section (*prapāṭhaka*).
Regarding the *saubhara*, *abhīvarta*, and *jaya* chants, one should desire the increase of the fourth [part] with the verse beginning "apiyūrvājā."

*madhudasma*, *anādyaṃ jaye*, *śyāvāśve*, *cāyāvāsvā somadhāma*, *saphapauṣkalayoḥ*, *ve hī*, *ṣyāmūne*, *dvipadāyāḥ*, *sakhā turīya*, *sye mahi*, *dvitīyamanvayikyām*, *ca mīṅkha*, *hraṅgiryaṃmimadimaghopāriṣṭe*, *rayībhṛthi triṣṭubhe ca*, *utāyā śane ca*, *dvitīyacaturthastham*, *ayatīṃyudhāte*, *de sye cātaye vakaḥ*, *sarvatrāntyam*, *apurandhi praśāsti*, *māndhādi śme'dhṛṣṇāsmānmadhorvṛṣṇāvasvīśca rave*.

In the *Yaudhājaya* [Sāman], the sixth syllable of the *Gha* [verse] is [the *nidhana*]; in the *Sarvamaraṇa*, the penultimate syllable; in the *Daivya*, the syllable *dā*; in the *Hauhacya*, the syllable *ho*; in the *Janitra*, the syllable *śṛ*; in the *Leya*, the syllable *le*; in the *Dvipadā*, the syllable *jñī*; in the *Vairūpa*, the second syllable from the end; in the *Prāhvāṅghra*, the syllable *añ*; in the *Asaṃyoga*, the syllable *ava*; in the *Avakayābhiḥ*, the syllable *su*; in the *Suśatrave*, the syllable *dhṛ*; in the *Soma*, the syllable *vā*; in the *Nihotṛ*, the syllable *ni*; in the *Nāsāddadhīn*, the syllable *mu*; in the *Mudra*, the syllable *na*; in the *Drasvabdi*, the syllable *ca*; in the *Kṛtyāniṣyata*, the syllable *ni*; in the *Mṛḍhvaṃ*, the syllable *ni*; in the *Hotāṇaḥ*, the syllable *so*; in the *Ayaṃmaghajñaiḥ*, the syllable *pa*; in the *Parikratuḥ*, the syllable *i*; and in the *Godanvate*, the syllable *mā*.

In the three [hymns] beginning with Cāgiri, in Traiśoka, in the first and last [of the two] in Aiṭata, in Sārathi, in Avigīta, in Vaiśvāmitra, in all [the hymns] in Neve, in the alternative [case] in Naikarca, in Yave, in Mahyāmarasam, in Pra, in the first and last of Anadru, in Gha, in Vaidhṛti, in Ci, in all [the hymns] in Janitra,
Saṃkṣāra, Rathira, and Ījeṣu, in Dyauta, in the middle of Anetṛca, in a four-syllable [verse], in Naikarca, and in the two following [hymns], [the word] gha [is used] in Yāma.

The *pṛśni* [stotra] begins with *apād*, the *bhādana* with *vibhiḥ*, the *apsuṣut* with *abhijit*, the *vajra-ādyādana* with *anut*, the *soma* with *yasyābhīśubhiḥ*, the *gītā* with *adri*, the *narṣaṇya* with *antaḥ*, the *āviḥ* with *yat*, the *daṃtaḥ* with *ro*, the *naudhasa* with *āidra*, and the *ānta* with *at*. The *napuṃsa* [stotra] is in a different meter (*vichandas*), and the *pūrva-alleya* [stotra] has a *prastāva* similar to the *ṛk*; the *turīya* [stotra] begins with *śipra*, and the *atisuta* with *adyayoḥ*. After *sthā*, there is no [following element] for the two subsequent [stotras]. In the *vrātya*, the *ṣkala-yoni*, and the *havya*, [the stotras begin] with *upaśipra*, *paripradhanva*, *sakha*, *prāṇa*, and *atṛca*. In the *śana*, the *svasvin*, and the first [of the] *vikalpa*, as well as in the *hiṣṭhīya*, [the rule is] *ama*.

In *pratṛjāpluta*, there is the elision of *va*; in *dvitṛtanīcaḥ* and *phe hatikṛṣṭāt*, [the same applies]; in *avṛddhaśyene*, *jigyuya*, *mavovṛpra*, *pratyavarohe*, and *śāktye*, [the rule applies] to *naya-jaye-hārāt-avitāṣabho-riyā*; in *tā vane*, [the rule applies] to that which begins with *hāra* when it consists of more than one verse (*anekarce*), and in *dādau*, *bhāvese*, *nau raścye*, *nitre*, and *tryante*; in *tvāṣṭrīsāmni*, *havye*, and *cāyonau*, [the rule applies] to *matsari*; the words [are applied] in *svāsūttarayoḥ*, *daivye*, *tsode*, *hāre*, *the*, *dhau*, *hāre*, *thāsye*, *devo*, *jayasāptamika*, and *triṇidhanāyāsyeṣu*.

The *hitānta* [is used] in the *sārvādirya-vākhyau*; the *ṣṭu* [is used] in the *śveta-pāṣṭhauha*; *soma* [is used] for the beloved in the *vārśa*; *soma* [is used] for the swift one who possesses power; *putra* [is used] in the *ākhādira-yoni*; *ṛddha* [is used] for the *iḍopāya*; the first [is used] in the *ādyā*; and also in the *udvaśīya*. The second [is used] in the *āndhīgava* and in the *asantu-svāra*; [it is used] in the *parṇeya-yoni*, in the *pṛṣṭhya*, and in the *ajiga-surūpa* [verses]; *vyamaśī* [is used] in the *gīthā-ādyakāva*; *te* [is used] in the *jñīya*; *punādeva* [is used] in the *svāsu*; the first [is used] elsewhere in the *pramaha-ādyayoḥ*; *bhādriṣṭāḥ* [is used] in the *śāṃma-tre*; and in the *vaiśvāmitra-kṛte*.

The fourth [syllable] is long everywhere; the sixth [syllable] is long in *dhvakṣayoḥ*, *pāje*, *the*, *bhe*, *dairghye*, and *pare*; it is long everywhere in *akakubhi*, *havye*, *tsivāyām*, and those beginning with *ayāt*; and it is long in *ghṛtanidhana* and *sāṃvartta* when they occur at the beginning of a verse-line.

In the *gharmṛga* and others, at the end of the *amasa*, and wherever it occurs after the *parā* [formula], I am not [the subject]; in the *vātsapra* and the fourth *pāda*, and in the long *triṣṭubh* and *paṣṭha*, and where there is *dīrgha*, and at the end of *syatraṣāṇī*, and in *kṣaudra*, the fourth [is applied]; likewise in *dhīgave*, the sixth [is applied]; in *pratyutkrāmati*, everywhere, and in the womb (*yonau*), in *paryūṣu*, *viśastvā*, *rittvaṃ*, *dyāṃca*, and in the *dvipadā*s, the first [is applied]; in *indrāsomābhidhā*, in the third, in *vārddhasyatanvā*, *rātāśatāt*, *abdhāyāṃ*, and in the middle of *tvāṃdhāma*.

In the *mānoca* [verse], the second syllable of the first line is drawn out; in the *aupahita*, the third syllable of the second line; in the *audalari*, the fourth syllable of the second line; in the white *sāman*, the fifth syllable of the second line; in the *āyāsya*, the sixth syllable of the second line; in the *saṃyoga*, the seventh syllable of the second line; in the *dvaigata*, the eighth syllable of the second line; in the *prasoma*, the ninth syllable of the second line; in the *anta*, the tenth syllable of the second line; in the *madhyamā*, the eleventh syllable of the second line; in the third [section], the twelfth syllable of the second line; in the two *bṛhatīs*, the thirteenth syllable of the second line; in the *hovā*, the sixteenth syllable of the second line is drawn out. In the *tvam agne*, the first syllable of the first line is drawn out; in the middle [line], the third; in the last [line], the fourth. In the *anuṣṭubh*, the first syllable of the first line is drawn out; in the two *śyena* verses, the second and seventh syllables of the first line; in the *kim* verse, the third syllable of the first line; in the *pūrva* verses, the fourth syllable of the first line; in the *tava* verse, the fifth syllable of the first line; in the middle [line], the sixth syllable is drawn out.

And in the *gośṛṅga* [stotra], in the eighteen *viśeṣṭubh* [verses], in the third [turn] at the end, beginning with *indra*, Soma [is praised]; in the eighth [turn] as before, in the *prīca* and *yajña* [sections], in the *randhra* and the preceding *sraugma* [sections], not in the *yoni*; in the *uta-dviṣā* [section], not in the *yoni*; in the *hinvaviśīya* [section], in the *āyithyā* [section], and at the beginning of the *yoni*; in one's own [verses], in the second foot of the second [verse], and in the last [verse], of the last [foot], in the *gītha* [portion]; in the *pāntyatrī* [verses], in the *bodhīya* [section], not in the *yoni*; in the *pravājyā* [section], at the beginning of the first [verse], and in the second foot of the *upāyā*; in the *kāṇva* [recension], in the *yoni*; in the *siṣṭha* [section], in the second *hāra*; in the *nada* [section], in the *purojiti* [section], and in the *haviṣ* [section].

In the *savājya* [verse], for purification, in the *cau* [verse], and in the *randhra* [verse], the first [part] is in the *uttamā*; the second in the *dhyamā*; the third in the *ādyā*, or in the *bodhīya*; the third [part] in the *gītha* of the first two *pravājyas*; the fourth is twice-drawn (*dviḥkṛṣṭa*) in the final [verse]; or in the *vāśedhya*, the last three of the feet; four [parts] in the *pibantam-ayantahivechandas*; one in the *aśveḥ-vāna-hojita*; "asmaiha śaṃthī syagnebhiḥ" [is sung] in the long [verse]; in the *vrātyāgniṣṭut*, the second and seventh [parts] are drawn in the *gītha*; in its own [verses], the second and sixth [are drawn]; the *prastāva* [is drawn] in the third; the fourth is in the *armṛ*.

The second [stotra] is on the *thamocca* [verse]; the third is on the *plīha*; the fourth is everywhere on the *kakubh*; the seventh is on the *vaiyaśva*; the fifth is on the two *uttara* [verses]; the eighth is on the single-verse (*ekarca*) [hymn], as well as the fourth *gītha*.

In the *tare*, *hārādi*, and *anuttara* [stomas], [the *nidhana*] is at the end of the *navagīthādi* verses; in the *rayau*, in *śoka*, and in the final two [stomas], it is in the *vichandas*; in the *āgneya*, in the *kakubh*, and in the *yonau sāmarāja*, it is at the end of the *pāda*; and in the *kāmpā*, it is at the beginning of the *pada* when there is a long vowel. It is not [used] in *jāgṛviḥ*, *devasya*, *kvacid*, *vāvṛma*, *arusūri*, *kāri*, *dāśuṣi*, or *rājani*. In *soma*, in the *sāman*, in the *treya*, in *rayā nausadharevatīṣu*, in *payasi*, in *parinogi*, in *ṣivamantotthayoḥ*, in *dhe dridaṣṭre*, in *sāsite*, in *samīmasruce*, in *havyehāradvitīyamapurojiprāntyayoḥ*, and in *nitre*, [the respective syllables are acute].

In the *purojima* and *madhyamā*, these [occur]; in the *triṣṭubh* at the end, the third and fourth [parts] of the *naiyegītha*, the first of the *ṣṭhauha*, the fifth of the *naucaka*, and the third in the *sāman*; in the *navṛddha*, the beginning of the *vasaṃkṛti* and *yaśas*; in the *vṛṇyādi* and *kamaśva*, [these occur] in the two following; in one's own [verses], the sixth; in the *devīviṣṭha*, the *ṣṭhā* in repetition; in the *manājyā*, the beginning of the *rāyi-rā* ending in *antya*; in the *jyā*, the second *udādi*; in the *ravaruṇā*, the *triṇidhana*; in the *āsyasvāno*, the *nitravat*; in the *triṣṭupsutsapre*, the *dādayaḥ*; and in the *puraujicā*, the beginning of the *vairāja* with repetition, and in the *hañcana*.
In all instances of *ahaṅgatā* and *abhīśava*, [the rule applies] to both *ahaṅgatā* and *abhīśava*. This is the fifth chapter (*prapāṭhaka*).

The vowel *aḥ* (long *ā*) is augmented when sung over a word-final position, provided it occurs before the suffixes *ghoṣa* and *kāra*. Regarding those of this class—such as *purohāitā*, *dhavādāivā*, *idāhāyā*, and *evaṃjātīyāni*—we shall now describe the *saṃdhyāgīta* (euphonic chanting). The word *madaḥ* is the first *svara* (accented syllable). In *pacasvaśaṅku*, it occurs in the second [verse]. In *matsyabṛhati*, *ca*, *tamadrivo*, and *yadidracitrāyām*, [it occurs] in the beloved [verse] of Vasiṣṭha. In *rathītaro*, *nakiṣṭvad-rathāmāyām*, *āsite*, *hiṣastve*, *somayaudhe*, and *payorjījanāyām*, [the same applies].

In *vāśve*, the *rasa* [melody] is used; in *svāsu*, *tamasoḥ*; in *arke*, *puronaḥpreddhaḥ*; and here in *marāye*, it is sung on the final syllable of the word (*bhaktyanta*). We shall explain the *saṃdhyagīta* (euphonic junction singing) everywhere. In *krauṃcāṣṭamike*, the [melody] is optionally applied to *uṣasaḥ abhi priya* and *vaikhānase*. In *dvigate*, [it is used for] *punānāyām* and *utsaḥ jigāti*. In *pūtāyām*, these two words *māma* and *ūrje* are used in *krauṃcāṣṭamike*. In *naudhasa*, the word *indraḥ* is used; in *kaīṃ vedāyām*, the word *āṣkāraṇidhane*; in *kāṇve*, the words *mahodivaḥ*; in *pratnaṃ pīyūṣāyām*, the word *yaudhe*; and in *prasmavājeṣu naścādhvaryavaḥ suvarvidaḥ*, these two words are used. In *ājāgṛviḥ*, it is used in *auśana*.

"Indraḥ śūraśca," "mahānāmnīṣu," "yadvārathobodhīye," "vārethāduvaehi," "ūtṛtīyāyāṃ," "numadrivaścabarhiṣaśca," "taṃtemadāyāsiṣāsaṃtaḥ," "śrudhīhavāyāṃ," "devarādhaḥ," "sadudravāyā," "rajaḥ sūryo," "vite," "mahaḥ," "stavāno bṛhadrathaṃtare," "pavitraṃvataiti devāsaśca," and "tryaṃtetvāṣṭrīsāmni."

In the *stobha* and *pratyaya*, there is *padagīta* in the middle of the *bhakti* and the middle of the *pāda*. We shall explain the *saṃdhyagīta* everywhere. [The following apply]: in *asya indraḥ*, *kṣāre*, *vasurucau*, *utsedhe*, *tuvaḥ*, *svārayoḥ*, *tvāṣṭrīsāman*, *rajaḥ*, *sūryaḥ*, and the two preceding [verses]; in *devodhauta*, *matsarāsaḥ*, *aśvañjambhe*, *vṛṣāmadaḥ*, *svare*, *bṛhan*, *nidhane*, *kyaḥsvāsu*, *vatsāsu*, *abhighucyāvanepāsāstham*, *pavasvamadhumāyām*, *indraḥ*, *śyenaḥ*, *saṃtani*, *somaḥ*, *vāmne*, *candraḥ*, *vābhre*, and *rādhaḥ* in the *kautsa*.
O God Soma, bring joy to the singers; being purified, flow for our welfare, bringing delight to both sides, you who are exhilarating.

In the *stobha*, the *bhakti* is in the middle and the *madhya* is in the middle; the *sandhyagīta* occurs in the *pratyaya*. I shall now describe the *padagīta* everywhere: [the word] "deva" at the end of the *pratyukta*; in the second [verse], "jigannava"; in the *pūtā*, "ste"; in the *krauñca*, "vāṅgidhane"; in the second [verse], "jāraḥ prasunvān"; in the *hīṣī* [svara], "tatsastriṇidhana"; in the *āsyā*, "ghṛtavratas"; in the *traiśoka*, "bharantaḥ"; in the *saubhara* and *leya*, these two words "purojinara"; in the *marāya*, "śucayemā"; in the *utvāyāśya*, "ete śvaḥ"; in the *kārttayaśa*, "audalasya veṣu".

*Śyenaḥ saṃmiślāyām*, *asahite jātā*, *vācaḥ sāmnī priyam devāyām*, *dadhanvān yaḥ sarvatra*, *dakṣa-śūrāvarke*, *śārṅge ca brahma-yujau*, *bhāradvāje purāṃ darma āmandrair ity atrābhinidhane*, *kāṇve martyo yo yaḥ sahotāyām*, *kamaśve aśvayant abhitvā śūrāyām*, *kaṇvatara asyed indraś ca abhitvā pūrvāyām*, *suṣṭutayo vaṣaṭtāyām bṛhati*, *ruṣaud yasya pṛta ity atra vājīye*, *divyo rathantare bṛhati*, *rādhastabhau vīṃke*.
O you who bring prosperity, for Indra, O Saubhara, bringing the offering, come hither; being purified, flow for the sake of strength, for the sake of the sacrifice, at every awakening.

The sound *ā* occurs in the *ākāra*; the word *pā* in the *prakāvyā*, *pārtha*, *vārāha*, *kutsa*, and *rathīya* hymns; *indrāya* and *indavit* in the *krauñca* hymn; in the *stobha* following the first two *stotrīyas*; in the *pratyaya* of *vāhāyi*; in the *jasā* and *vaiśvamanasa* hymns; in the *vṛdhā*, *bṛhat*, and *bhāra* hymns; in the *pūrvathā* and *kaṇvatara* hymns; in the *dvitā* and *sujñāna* hymns; in the phrase *diva āpratnam pīyūṣam*; in the *jaya*, *mahīyava*, and *utsedha* hymns; in the *uccaiḥ* and *neṭana* hymns; in the *ekāra* *pratyaya*; in the *ārya*, *kāleya*, and *āsāt* hymns; in the second and last [verses]; in the *jetā*, *nārmedha*, *havya*, and *viśīya* hymns; in the *indrātoka* and *vārṣāhara* hymns; and in the *gītha* and *abhyāsa* *pratyayas*.

In the *huhā-sakhā* [verse], when there is the suffix *-mat*, the vowel *ā* becomes *āḥ*; in the *madāḥ* [verse], when there is the suffix *-suta-* in connection with *soma-*, it becomes *āḥ* in the praise (*stava*) of the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara* [Sāmans]; in the *tamāḥ* [verse], in the *śyāva-kṣāśva* [verse], and in the suffix *-vāyām*, it remains as *ā*; in the *nityavat-sātīṣaṅga-simā* [verses], the vowel *i* becomes *u* in the *utsedha* [verse]; in the *duhānā* [verse], in the *pratīni-dvi-hikā-devī* [verse], and in the *arṣasi-kaṇva-tareḍin* [verse], when there is the *āstobha* suffix in the latter two [sections], the vowel *o* becomes *u*; in the *nadaṃva-ūsat-gastobha-stobha* [verse], and in the *mahām-idam* [verse], the vowels *e* and *au* become *a*; and in the *oṣṭhya* [verse], in the *mahe-jñīya* [verse], the vowel *ī* becomes *ā*. And for us...

In the *Arṣasipunānīya*, in the *Sāptamika* and *Triṇidhana* [chants], in the *Yaudhājaya*, in the *Vṛṣo acikradat* and the *Triṇidhana*, in the *Ayaṃ pūṣā* and the *Krauñca*, in the *Bṛhatstoma*, in the *Parotsedha*, in the *Duhānā*, in the *Purumatsva*, in the *Pratyaya*, and in the *Vairāja*, the first vowel-sound (*svara*) is the word "puruṣaḥ" among the *vyāhṛtis*. And in all [these] *kāma* [chants], the word "madabhīruha" occurs in the middle; this is the alternative.

In the case of the suffixes *ṣa* and *sparśa*, when preceded by *vṛddha*, *ṛ*, *vaṇ*, *dga*, or *sarva*, words ending in *ghna* become *ār*—such as *kārmāṅkā* and *dvī*. However, the vowel *ṛ* does not become *ār* before all *sparśa* consonants, as in *yājñāritṝbhyaḥ*, *maghavāotṛ*, and *pātṛ*. The vowel *ṛ* becomes *ār* before the suffixes *ta* and *ṣa*, as in *tārttāyām*, *adhiro*, and *tārṣāṇā*. The vowel *oṃ* becomes *ū* before *gṛ*, *hṛ*, *pṛ*, *śṛ*, *ṅgā*, *rh*, and *pā*, as in *rucaduṣasaḥ*, *pārśniḥ*, *agrāyārayāme*, and *cāyaṃgauriti*. The suffix *na* is not mentioned here, but it occurs after the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).

There is the elision of the consonant in *śvonakā* and *śconakā*. Regarding what was stated previously—that the vowel *ā* occurs before the suffixes *sakāra* and *sparśa*—there are exceptions therein: *sasṛgmavāvṛdhācanārmedhe*, *cakṛmāśāktya*; this very same example applies to *yūthādānāyāṃ*, *kaulmakaṇvabṛhatoḥ*, and *saṃgṛbhānnaḥ* in *ākūpāre*. This very same example applies to *marmṛsvāsudairgha* in *abhikraṃdāyāṃ*, *dhenuvaruṇayoḥ*, *girastaiṃdāyāṃ*, and *sadgahite*. [The rule applies] in *nabhṛprasunvānāyāṃ*.

In the case of Gautama, Sādhra, Śyāvāśva, Audala, Ākūpāra, Dāsa, Vaiśvāmitra, Svāra, Kautsa, Karāvata, and Dohitara, [the rule applies] to the *nṛbhiḥ pratta* and *gāsadhastha* [verses]. In this regard, the examples are the same for Aiḍa, Udyāsya, Goghnīya, Ṣedha, Ābhīśāṣka, Āra, Soma, Varuṇa, Tamatara, and Jambha. [The rule applies] to *abhisomā*, *dhyāsyāt*, *gahaduttha*, and *agner triṇidhana*. In *hanman*, [it applies] to the *dharttā* [verse], the *jñīyaka*, and the *abhikranda* verses; and in *avadyutānā*, as well as in *tamaso arke*.

This very [verse] is an illustration for *kakubha* in the *madāya* [meter], *gāhāri*, *bhara*, and *vāra*; furthermore, it is to be known as an example for *punaḥ* in the *punānā* [meter], for *tam* in the *madā* and *sadgṛhīta* [meters], and for *proṣu* in the *vatsā* [meter].

In the *samṛtra-aiśauka*, in the *vṛktavaya-ghatvāyāma-abhinidhana*, in the *kāṇva-vṛṣṇi*, in the *yatsānor-vadgaśīya-iva-upadṛk-upatvājā-vāra*, in the third [chapter], this very same example occurs in the *ayadgas-sūryāyāmāmahīyava-bodhīya-ṛṣabhā-apāvamāna-aśumārgī-saumyaiṭata-sākeghṛṣikṛt-śiśudevyādve-jyotiṣa* sections; in the three [verses] of the *pāhiraurava*, in the *syapurukṛt-chagvyūhāramānava-yo-rurukṛt-dukuvit-sunāyāṃ-bodhīya-pṛthivīṃ-pradaivyaṃte-bṛhat* sections, and in the *yajjāyathāyā*.

In the *mṛdhak-soma-davi-jñīya*, the vowel *ṛ* becomes *vṛddhi*. Furthermore, in the *ārbhava*, in the words *ṣaṭ*, *bhūmi*, *dhṛṣṇu*, *vṛṣṇi*, *vṛṣan*, *vāre*, *mṛtyu*, *dhenau*, *kṛ*, *evate*, *krauñcam*, *mṛjya*, *kaevatare*, *kṛtam*, *śakuni*, and *mārjyamānaḥ*, as well as in *suhastiyān*, *nirgāḥ*, *akārtadaḥ*, *tṛmpāyām*, *ṛvarṇam*, *prāptat*, and *garephaḥ*, when a *vṛddhi* vowel occurs in the first syllable, it is designated as such; and in the *trāpā-stha-tare*, in the *pūrva-devya-hṛd-āgneya* verses, when the vowel *ṛ* is reached, it is changed to *arkāra*, and not otherwise.

We shall explain those vowel-conjunctions (*svarasandhi*) which are joined within a *pāda* of a *ṛc*, and those which are open in a *sāman*: *maddvevasa*, *imā uvāyāṃ*, *vāṃradevyarathabṛhatsu*, and *śrudhye tu*—these are joined; *abhīndramabhivāyum* here [is joined] at the end of the *pārtha*; *ketavaḥ svāsu*, *mahatā garbho*, *mahattatsomāyādgasa*; however, in all *chandas*, there is joining: *prasunvānāyādgasa*; in all cases, *pavasvayaste madāyādgasa*; in all *soma-sāmans*, there is joining in the *śāṃmade*s: *puronaḥ* in all cases.

In the case of *māsiḥ*, *māśivāsaḥ*, and *sarvatra ścādrinārvācaḥ*, there is elision (*praśleṣa*) before *piba somāya* and *amṛṣabhe*; in *prasmavājeṣu naḥ sarvatra*, there is elision before *ravodgīthe*; in *navibhiḥ suṣāva somāyādga sarvatra*, there is elision; and in *aṣṭādaṅgaṣṣṭrārkapuṣyasaṃkṛtiyaśaḥsu*, there is elision (*praśleṣa*).

In the *sute cit* [verse], in the *anave vṛddha*, and everywhere in the *āyāsya*, there is a *praśleṣa*; in the *kaṇvabṛhatī* according to the former ritual manual (*kalpa*), in the *stotra* "udindra tvadgatyehi," in the *jambha* as the *pratihāra*, and in the *kaulma* *stotra*; in the *gāyatoyūthādānāyāṃ kaṇvabṛhatī*, in the *jambha*, and in the first [verse] of the *vairāja* "tavādyāyadgasahodairghamarāyayoḥ" in the *stotra*; in the second [verse] of the same, in the *ābhīśava* and *vaigata*, and in the *rahasya*; in the *bṛhatī* [verses] "aruṣī," "pratiṣyā," and "sūnarī" in the second [verse]; and in the *bodhīya* [verse] "devājaramāte agne."

In the phrase *idhīmahi*, [the svarita] occurs before *tvam* and *na* in the case of *aindraupagave*; in the case of *asādvantīya*, it occurs before the last syllable of the third foot; in *mā praprayobha* and *yadi indrāya adri śyene*, it occurs in the *ṛcatovairāja-ṛṣabha* [meter]; in *daivāñjasā bṛhati*, it occurs before *mahīnadhārā* and *gorājā* in the *kāva* [meter]; and the *svarita* following the final syllable of a foot is drawn out (*vikṛṣyate*), as in *yathā nūṣata avadyutānāyāśācipūjanāyam ta indra*. In the second foot of [the verse], it occurs in *dakṣāya vidharmaṇi* and *gamiṣṭhān asaskṛtam*; such are the cases in the *auśana* [school].

Now follow the exceptions (*apavāda*). Regarding the word *aṃśoḥ*, there is a coalescence (*praśleṣa*) after an unvr̥ddha vowel; this applies everywhere here except in the following cases: in *yad indra citrāyām*, in *vasiṣṭhapriya-ṣaṅgayoḥ*, in *divas-pade-tayoḥ*, in *apavitrāyām*, in *jñīye*, in *mo ṣu tvā pārśve*, in the repetition of the word *śrudhi*, in *dhiyo agne bharāma idhmāyām* at the end, in *jiṣu-santanini-tvic-i-suṣvāṇāyām*, in *āṃdhāṃ-gaveṃ-dhasaḥ*, in *staṃ vo dasmādyāyām*, in *ātharvaṇa-saubharayoḥ*, and in *pratyasmai tṛtīyāyām*.

In the *Rathantara*, [the words] "avāsṛjo rātayaḥ" occur; these two words [are found] in the *Proṣu vatsāsaḥ*, in the *Yujāṇiḥ*, in the *Siṣāya*, in the *Raurava*, in the *Bodhaya*, in the *Mahenā*, in the *Vājīya*, in the *Iḍiteva*, in the *Sotra*, in the *Kakubha*, in the *Tamoṣā*, in the *Varṇa*, in the *Arcatapriye*, in the *Brahmayujā*, in the *Kakṣe*, in the *Dhasodraya*, in the *Vātsapra*, in the *Nadīdhimaḥ*, in the *Śrāyantā*, in the *Asaubhara*, in the *Sainya*, in the *Osi bārhadgirasa*, in the *Saṃtaninaḥ*, in the *Vāhanaḥ*, in the *Agnervivasvat*, in the second [verse], in the *Śrudhya*, in the *Vṛṣṇi*, and in the *Udyasyate*—here in the *Vājīya*, in the *Dhārayāsedhe*, in the *Dhiyosedhe*, in the *Jamavartta*, and in the *Agnetaṃ adya kamaśve*. In the *Tatarditha*, in the *Dairgha*, in the *Śravasyavaḥ*, and in the *Daivya*.
Regarding the divine union of those seeking glory (*śravasyava*):

wherever there is a combination of *y* and *v*, it is sometimes contiguous and sometimes separated; therein, the contiguous [occurrence] is found in *nyaryaḥ*, *sāhīya*, *parṇa-varṇa*, *mitra-vilambeṣu*, *naiḍe*, *divyam*, *jyarṣasi-yaśaḥ-sasarpapuṣyeṣu*, *āpṛcchyam*, *avṛddha*, and everywhere in *madeṣu*. In the *ākūlīya*, [it occurs in] *jihyūṃ-kṛt-nyaś-ca*. In the *jñīyasya udgītha*, [it occurs in] *viśvācyā-aśvinoḥ-vrata-paryākūpāra-puṣya-marāyeṣu*. In the repetition (*nābhyāse*), [it occurs in] *tvat-ryaś-ca*; and in these, in the *vaighena* and *amarāye*, [it occurs] in *tvagnaye-svāsu*.

In the verse *dairghaidhyamāyāsūryasyābhipriyāṇi*, this very word [sūrya] occurs in the *svāraka* and *vajñīya* [chants]. In the verses containing *sūrya* belonging to *iṣu* and *rājadvitīyā*, and in the *auśana* [chant], as well as in *atisūrya*, *puṣyam*, and *arāyakīrtti*, the word *indra* [occurs]; in *sūryasrucanaiyakīrtti*, it is like *sūrya*; and in *baṇmahāasi*, the word *sūrya* occurs everywhere. However, in the *vitanaiya* [chants], the first [word] is drawn out (*vikṛṣṭa*) in *sūrye*. In *mahattat* and *somāyāṃ*, in the *vaiśvajyotiṣa* and *vātsapra* [chants], and in the *āmāyāmā* [chant], the word *sūrya* occurs everywhere; in the *asya pratnāyām* [verse], the word *ayasūrya* occurs.

In all these cases, specifically here in the third [chapter], [the word *sūrya*] does not occur in *sūryo bhrāje*, nor in *sūryasya nata gireḥ*. In this [section], *mahīsūryaḥ* is for the sake of praise (*kīrttyai*). In *sasūryasyeha vāmam*, *sūryā vairūpām antarikṣayoḥ*, *tu asūrya saumitre*, *samusūrya saṃtanini*, and in the *parvan* sung according to the *ṛc*, [it occurs]. In *avitād āśe mahāyām*, in *jñīya-viśīya-vāra-mahāmitratara*, in *etadyūka maśve*, in *tvām iddhi avibhare*, in *tvāya sarvatra vyābhiḥ*, in *nārmmedhe*, in *kuṇḍapāyyaḥ sadmane vyomani*, and in *indrasutāyām*.
In the previous aeon, those who were masters of themselves impelled the waters with the *hiṃkāra*, like a cow lowing, in the most excellent and further-reaching [sacrifices].

In the *nyau* [metres], there is *taṃ tvā dharttāya āha*; in the *aviṣmat* and *santani*, it is optional (*vibhāṣā*). In the second [verse] of the *prasunvat*, there is *rathantara idā hyo mānave syupamā chandase pūrvyo vṛṣā matī dvitīyāyāṃ jñīye tvām abhidaṣṭrottare*. In the *magha*, *dvihiṅka*, *hārabhāra*, *māna*, *uttara*, and *rauratare*, there is *utasyuḥ*. In the *vairūpa*, *antarikṣa*, and short [verses], there is *vṛṣṭi-ayā-vairūpe*. In the second [verse] of the *haryaśva-piba-soma*, there is *saho dairghye marāyai tvādya-yoḥ syanta-mā-marāyai vidvān marāyava-vairāja-ṛṣabha-yoḥ*.

*tvā* in *bhūrihitāyām*, *marāye*, *sahodairghye*, *tvabhyāsaḥ*, *naptyoḥ*, *aurṇāyavayoḥ*, *paripriyāyām*, *mārgīyave*, and *ca tvahyā*; these two words [tvā and hyā] in *sauparṇye*, *pavitramati*, and *ejñīye*; *na* in *kiṣṭvat*, *site*, and *asāvyaśuḥ*; everywhere except in *santanini*; *pāṣyoḥ*, *krośe*, *ṣyaiḥ*, *ayata*, *aita*, *krośa*, and *vārśeṣu*; *tvaritvam* and *ghām* in *gavāṣṭeyu*, *simāsu*, *tvam*, *ghām*, *śuddhīye*, *suhasti*, *arandhra*, *uttara*, *varuṇagoṣṭha*, and *arkapuṣpeṣu*; and *svānaḥ* in *parisvānāyām*.

In the *vaidanvatā*, *haviṣmatī*, and *revatī* verses, this very word [is used]; in the *akrān* verse of the *Vasiṣṭha* family, and in the *parītat* and *adhyāsyā* verses on the ninth day; in the second [day], in the *danvate* verse, in the *mitrāḥ svā nāḥ* verse everywhere, in the *dadhi-āśiraḥ-vite* verse, in the *vyadribhir-yajñīye* verse; in the *tvaṃ mātā* verse of the *Upagu* family, in the *vareṇyam* and *prarādhyam* verses, in the *atīṣaṅga* verse, in the *atyogabhasti* verses, and in the *jñīya* verse—the word *svaḥ*; in the *svaḥ-kāvābhikrandayoḥ* and *ratyoḥ* verses, in the *atyogabhasti* verses, in the *ṣvāviśe* verse—these three words [are used] in the *Śārṅga* verse;
in the *kṛtvī-anumāghoḥ* and *atyogabhasti* verses, and in the *svaḥ-ṣvāviśa* verses—these six words [are used] in the *Eṣaḍa* verse.
Thus ends the sixth Prapāṭhaka.
The seventh Prapāṭhaka begins:

In the *saṃkṣāra* for the gods, in the *narya*, in the *parītā*, in the *mādhuyā*, in the *asyabhīśa*, in the *auradaṣṭra*, in the *jaṃbhānūpra*, in the *udhadvaigaṇvatara*, in the *sthānasaṃkṛti*, in the *bhargayaśa*, and in the *atharvaṇatara*—on the ninth day, everywhere except for the *dairgha*, there is an option (*vibhāṣā*) regarding the *aruṇasāmnya*; this same word is *saṃkṛṣṭa*. In the *gomannaṣkala*, in the *iṣṭyavyadvyabhyālauśe*, and in the *tamasorke*—here itself, on the third [day], the final one is everywhere [used] in the *nyojasākīrtya*, in the *bhyaṃ*, in the *kīrttya*, and in the *kāśītahāviṣkṛta*; this is the *svaśabda*.

In all [verses], the two words "tvā devāsaḥ" and "pīti" belong to the *vaiśvamanasa* and *śrudhya* [stomas]. In the *udvaśīya* and *vitaya* [stomas], they belong to the *sānvāruha*. In the *vaśīya*, *bhūri-vaśīya*, and *leyavita* [stomas], they belong to the *paryūṣvan*. In both the *andhīgava* and *stobha*, they belong to the *atardhya-vita*. In the *rājya*, *indhīgava*, and *daivya* [stomas], they are constant (*sanitya*) everywhere. In this very [context], in the third [stoma], in the *nvāśa-daivya*, the two words "npṛṇvan" and "dakṣāpya" belong to the *marāya* and *śepyā-bhāradvāja* [stomas].

In the *Ṣaḍiḍa* [Sāman], the word *vyasthiran*; in the *Avantya*, the words *svāraṅkāva*; in the *Jñāyaya*, the two words *tvam indra tvam indrasya*; in the *Yaśas*, the two words *vṛtrāṇi indrasya*; in the *Bṛhasya*, these two words; in the *Dvihiṃkāra*, the word *devye*; in the *Cartva*, the word *anyeyaśasi*; in the *Hasyabhīvarta*, the word *ṣvapitolauśe*; in the *Suvīra*, the word *śyene*; in the *Vyaśabda*, the word *śiśu*; in the *Devya*, the word *jyotiṣayoḥ*; in the *Putrebhyaḥ*, the word *bhāradvāje*; in the *Pratyaśabda*, the word *nānatarayoḥ*; in the *Yujyāviśīya*, the word *vratānyasya*; in the *Śyaitavājīya*, the word *pūrvyam*; in the *Utsedha*, the word *spṛkvabhiḥ*; in the *Pārśva*, the word *hariṇyāsatāsyebhir*; and in the *Vatsā*, the word *vatsāsu*.

The words *tve*, *somābhyam*, and *abhihi* [occur] in the *Dairgha*; *ghnyān*, *āśrudhye*, and *pṛṇadhvam* in the *Kaṇvatara*; *jātam*, *āryajñīye*, *pāhi*, and *utvām* in the *Iccaraurava*; *hyagnibhiḥ*, *caraṃtyaḥ*, *stāve*, *naiye*, *duryam*, and *tyudyatā* in the *Āndhīgava*; *nyaiḥ*, *ayajñīye*, *tvāndūtaḥ*, *jñīye*, *śagdhi*, *ūhāramānavayoḥ*, *stvaḥ*, *hyehi*, *jambhe*, *tvam*, *purūkaulmajambhayoḥ*, *pratyayakīrtye*, *ryaḥ*, *kāleye*, *pūryāḥ*, *saṃjaye*, *vīryasya*, *ṇyasyavāre*, *śrudhīhavāyām*, and *mādyepṛṣṭhe*.

In friendship, O hearer, here for these two; *tyūmāḥ*, *pūrvam*, *vyanaṭ*, *vet*, *ekam*, *anu*—these words are used in the *śyai* [section]; and the word *haryaśva* is used in the *pārya* [section]. In the *devya* [section], *vāvṛdhena* and *anyat*; in the *devya* [section], *satrācyān*, *kiṣṭvā*, *yoṣati*, *ācavāśe*, *sasadyat*, *ved*, *devāt*, *antyāt*, *yān*, *dūśmasi*, *amante*. *Tvamaṅga*, *kakubhe*, *vyuṣāḥ*, *kāve*, *mahatsu*, *āsaṃtanini*, *vīrasenyaḥ*, *saṃtani*, *hadgirayaḥ*, *roṣadhībhyaḥ*, *jñīya*, *matsyavṛhati*, *dadhe*, *vāryāṇi*, *kamaśve*, *svarṇajyotiḥ*, *uttare*, *kamaśve*.

In the *āśrudhya* [section], the word "sva" is indicated; in the *vāha* and *āhāra* of the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara*, the words "vṛṣṇi" and "āviṣṭavana" are used; in the *nidhana*, the word "kāvya" is used; in the repetition, these three words—"tvām," "vṛtreṣu," and "indra gāmaśvam"—are used; in the *vāra*, the word "tvām"; in the *kāṣṭhāsu*, the word "pratihāre"; in the *Bṛhat*, the word "tvā" in the seven days; in the *Indrabṛhatara*, the two preceding words "tvā" and "śabdau"; in the *pūrvoṣu*, the word "indratvajambhe"; in the *janitrī*, the word "aśyene"; in the *vīryaiḥ*, the word "devyabṛhato"; in this very [context], the word "kāmyam" in the *devye sakhye*;
and the word "sphigyam" in the *rathaṃtare yāme*; and the word "vyakhyat" in the *svovā rathaṃtare*.
