In the *aiṣkārasya* [section] before a *bhaisvara* suffix, there is elision of the *visarga* in *grahaṇair*, *bisargalopaḥ*, *sthābhir*, *yaste*, *surūpe*, *śyatir*, *abhidyunna*, in the third [verse], in *vācaḥ*, in *sāmni*, in *bhiḥ*, in *svāsu*, in *viśīye*, *śuciḥ*, in *paripriyāyām*, in *mārgīyave*, *gaviḥ*, in *prasomadāyām*, in *kaṇvatare*, *sutiḥ*, *pibātvasya*, in the *abhinidhanakaṇva* [section], in *nṛbhir*, *dadiriṃdro*, in *madāyām*, in *vārhadrir*, in *araśmayoḥ*, *varīḥsvāsu*, *raśme*, *gireḥ*, *vṛṣṇi*, in *jyotistāve*, in *pratyubṛhati*, and in *somasyatiḥ* before a suffix beginning with *h*.

In the *sahasradhārā* [hymn], in the *tvāṣṭra* and *sāman* chants, in the *svaraprathama*, in the *ariṣṭa*, in the *anāda*, in the repetition (*abhyāsa*) of the word *vadrir*, in the suffix (*pratyaya*) of *krāyām*, in the *vaiśvajyotiṣa*, *vātsapra*, and *arka* hymns, in the words *naki* and *nakiṣat*, in the word *rathāsva*, and in the suffixes of the *gaurīvita* and *asita* [sāmans].

In the case of the syllable *uḥ* followed by the suffix *auho*, there is elision of the visarga when it occurs with the *grahaṇa*s. [These occur] in the *pṛthu* [sāman], in the *sāṃvarta* [sāman], in the *kratu* [sāman], in the *parītādhyāsyā* [sāman], in the *āyāsya* [sāman], three times in the *tritā* [sāman], in the *vārśa* [sāman], in the *paripriyā* [sāman], and in the *mārgīyava* [sāman]. In the phrase *kasur indrakratum*, [the rule applies] in the *ṣṭambha*, *śyaita*, and *tanitra* [sāmans]; in the *durddharttā* [sāman], in the *vāsiṣṭha* [sāman], and in the *rahasya* [sāman]; in the *yodhābṛhat* [sāman], in the *vājayuḥ* [sāman], in the *sadovanā* [sāman], in the *antarikṣa* [sāman], in the *sajūr agne bṛhat* [sāman], and in the *visarjanīyakāraujīrāḥ* [sāman]. In the *saiṃdhukṣita* [sāman], in the *nikāma* [sāman], in the *avitaśṛṅga* [sāman], in the *jyākāḥ* [sāman], and in the *proṣu* [sāman].

In the *vatsa*, *asvakāroga*, and *gomanna* [sections], the *samudra* [section] is to be heard first; in the *svarai* [section], the word *svaḥ* occurs before both the *autvāya* and *aitanaudhasa* [sections]. When the word *sva* is joined with the preceding [syllable], its elision is performed according to the *atihāra* rule. Furthermore, in the *siṣṭha* and *traishoka* [sections], when joined with the subsequent [syllable], and in the case of *marāya* in the repetition (*abhyāsa*), some maintain that there is elision of the *visarjanīya* in the suffix (*pratyaya*) at the pause (*virāma*).

There is the elision of the letter *t* in *uchabdaḥ* in the *pārthuraśma*; in *yadyudīrāyām*, in *milāṃde*, and in *varce* when followed by the suffix *pratyaye*; in *parimarddhiṣat* in *svāsu*; in *hārāyaṇe*; in *dṛḍhācit* in *svāsuvīṃke*; in *bhāse* when followed by the suffix *pratyaye*; in *vovitsan*; in *indrāyāsaumitra*; in *iṃdromadāya*; in *amicchabdaḥ* in the *pārthuraśma*; in *id* in the *hiṃkārajñīya*; in *tvamindra* in the *paritya*; in *yud* in the *vaiśvāmitra*; in the third verse of *prasunvānatī*; in *tavet* in *pratyubṛhati*; there is the elision of the letter *m* in *utsannakaṃdaiḥ*; in *ghebhyabhihi* here; in *māsūryam*; and in *āyāsye* in the seventh [chapter].

In *tavāyām*, *manīṣām*, *kṣaudreṣu*, *sahodaiḥ*, *dīrgham*, *arāyavaḥ*, *rājarṣabheṣu*, *srasāma*, *iṭate*, *abhyāse*, *pratyaye*, *saīm*, *trikabṛhati*, *praprīm*, *yajñābṛhatyukāralopaḥ*, *upadṛg*, *ayasūryāyām*, *iṭataḥ*, *uta viṣṇoḥ*, *ca*, *janitāyāḥ*, *aśyāvāśve*, *yakāraḥ*, *pariṣṭobhantī*, *etasmin śabde*, *davijñīye*, *vāśabdaḥ*, *saphe*, *priyam devāyām*, *prathama-tṛtīyayoḥ vikalpayoḥ*, *akāraḥ*, *sanemitvāyām*, *adevaśrudhi*, *atraitaṣkaleṣu*, *aghāyoḥ*, *vāre*.

In the first [syllable] of *andhasaḥ*, *kṣullaka-*, *andhīgavaḥ*, and *vṛddhāt*; in *akṣara-dvaidhanvate* in the first [syllable]; in *advayi*, *simāsu*, *akṣaran*, *nakra-vastvaṣṭri*, and the first [syllable] of *agnaye-jñīya*; the letter *ā* [is elided]; in *taṃ tvā viprāya*, *am iha vat vāme*, the letter *i*; in *pra somāśve*, the consonant [is elided]; in the latter part [of a word], at the pause (*virāma*), it is elided, as is [the vowel] in reduplication (*abhyāsa*); in *normayoḥ*, *ṇasā*, *arjuna*, and *ṛbhvasaḥ*; likewise in *amṛtācārkaḥ*; the nasalized (*anunāsika*) letter *ān*; the *vṛddhi* [vowel] everywhere; in *are-vavai-ravāna-sasaṃtaniṣu*.

Everything separated by *āu* becomes *āu*, and the final consonant of a word is dropped. [Examples include: *śātāu-āu-bhavā*, *siyau-vā-u-grāu-vā-śarma-mahau-vā-yūjāu-vā-vājeṣu-cau-vā-madhāu-vā*. Words of this kind become *anāu*. [In the case of] Bhṛgu, *eva-tare*, *retaḥ-śyeneṣu*, *manaḥ-santaniny-aśiśrayuḥ-pravad-bhārgave*, and *aiṣṭhyaś-cāntaḥ-padikaḥ*, it becomes *nāu* everywhere. As in: *māndīm-ādāyatau-āu-vā*, *śrīṇanto-gobhir-ū-āu-vā*, *marut-ca-na-yoniḥ-soma-sāmni-sīdacchaye-na*.

Hāyina, āyāva, nāī, māuva, listen to this: the leafy wave of the *vāma* tree belongs to Medhātithi; like the roar of a bull among the *svarṇas*, the *sadasyas*, and the *vapras*, he has ascended the high mountains. Among the touches, there is no loss, as if it were the splendors of men; with thousands, with the sacrificial offerings, with the honey-sweet, with heroic power, they have surpassed those who were greedy for ghee. Like a hawk, like a leader, he has gone toward the heavens; he has sat down, he has stood up—the child, the Soma, the king of kings, the lord of the people. And in the secret place, not everything becomes manifest.

And the consonant is not elided, as in *vājī yan*, *nityavatsā*, *atīṣaṅgāḥ*, and *simāsu*. Where there is both the absence of the vowel and the elision of the consonant, that we shall explain: [the word] ending in a vowel, guttural, occurs everywhere, as in *viṣṇave sahasriṇam*. In the case of *yaṇ* and *vāpatya*, in *rañjoḥ* and *raivatayoḥ*, there is *vyamaḥ* and the letter *kāra*; in the *raivata* *simās*, everything becomes *āū* at the end of a verse (*anṛgante*) in the Vedic (*chāndasīṣu*) [passages]. In *diśo vasorāṇām*, there is the elision of the *gho* in the words ending in *mṛg* when followed by suffixes containing vowels or voiced sounds, as in *jyokkaḥ*.

In the *utvāha* [chant], there is the elision of the letter *s* in *śravastamaḥ*; in *sāhvān viśvāyāsahite*, [the elision occurs] with excellent praises (*suśastibhiḥ*). In the second [verse], in *mānastoke 'bhimājam āvartethāḥ*, there is elision at the beginning; it is either a secondary member (*parāṅga*) or [the elision of] *suhastāstāve*. In the *jñīya* [chant], there is elision; it is either a secondary member or [the elision of] *indrā yendav iti*. In the *krauñca* [chant], there is elision of *saṃ*; in the *sandhi*, there is movement (*gati*) when followed by a pause (*virāma*) joined with two *y*s. When [the *y*] is drawn out (*vikṛṣṭe*), the preceding *y* becomes a protracted (*pluta*) *ā*. In *rayisomaśravā ā yāṃyikrauñce*, because of the *nidhana* quality, [it becomes] *tyāvāmānā śravā yīyāṃ*.
In the *kuṇḍapāyya* and the *mahānāmnī*, after the word *praṇapāt*—whether it occurs in *kuṇḍapāyyāyāḥ* or in *satyaśravasi*—the vowel *i* arises from the *avṛddha-stobha*;
likewise, in the *rāyi somaśravau hovā hāiyām*.

An *anusvāra* followed by a consonant (*sparśa*) belonging to its own class, as well as a *repha* (the sound *r*), a consonant (*sparśa*), or a sibilant (*ūṣman*) joined with these, are all elided everywhere when they occur within a word (*antaḥpadika*), provided they are not separated by *stobha* syllables. There is elision at the end of a *stobha* or at a pause (*virāma*). In the case of euphonic combination (*saṃdhi*), there is no elision in the word *barhiṣi*. In such cases as *tarturāṇāḥ*, *piśaṅgam*, *īśānakṛt*, *aghaśasaḥ*, *sarāham*, and *mahā*, the consonant that would otherwise undergo elision due to the rule of *ati-hāra* is dropped. [This applies] in *ānaśadevye*, *jyotīṣi*, *vṛṣaṃ na*, *dadarśivāre*, *varpasā darśate*, *ilān*, *indhasaḥ*, *svāre*, and *parṇe*.

They praise at the *viśīya*; they urge on the two [singers] at the *viśīya* while exhilarated by the songs; they know the law regarding the progenitor at the *dairgha*. O best of sages, O drops (*indavas*), [this applies] at the *udvaśīya*, at the *karma*, at the *vatsāsu*, and at the *ārthavaṇa*; all that has been stated [applies] at the *ukthārtayaśas*. At the end of a *svara*, some [hold it to be] ending in a *visarjanīya* at the *svāsu*. One should bring the *tura* in the *bhara*; there is elision of the preceding member. Some [hold that] the elision of a word-final [consonant] which was reached is superseded; some [hold that] the word-final [consonant] which was reached is superseded by the preceding member due to the explicit statement. Before the *stobha*, the end of the *svara* is the pause; at the end of the *stobha*, [there is the pause].

In the case of *virata*, there is elision; in the case of *sandhi*, there is non-elision (*alopa*). [The following apply]: in *niṣṭhā*, *adhyadimāyā*, *sado-viśīya-utsedhayoḥ*, *kuvit-svāsu*, *mārgīyave*, *acikradat-pavamāna-abhyarṣasi*—in these instances, when there is no intervening *ka* or *vaṇ*, [the rule applies]. In *puram ajījanohi devye*, *maduritāya adadat devyaḥ*, *uṣarbudho agne vivasvat devye*, *girvaṇas tvayā bhūṣanti mānave*, *satpatim indraṃ viśvāyām*, *leye jambhe*, and in *catvā id dhi*—in these cases, when there is no intervention by *madhya-mā* or *āvā*, [the rule applies]. In *chidram aidhām jorūpeṣu* and *ṛtam āvā vyavahitam*, [the rule applies].
In *pārśva-santā-chidram aidhām jorūpa-agneḥ triṇidhaneṣu*, [the rule applies].

In the *śavasaḥ saṃjaya*, in the *sarad* for Gautama, in the *niṣkṛta-ruṇa-sāmnivṛṣa-cikrā*, in the *vayumapaghna* at *yavasāyām*, for Kākṣīvata they desired the *dhyama*; in the *marut-pavamāna-rathītama*, in the *kūlīya-santaniṣabha*, in the *dūrādvaṃtīya*, in the first *rasa*, in the *mārgīyava*, in the *hayattva-soma-aśiśāṃmada*, in the *drisavarddhitā*, in the *vitaśṛṅga*, in both types of *svāsu*, in the *maidhātitha*, in the *saṃpavitrā*, in the *sāmarāja*, that which was born in the second [verse], in the *bṛhat-rathaṃtara*, and wherever the word *yat* occurs—therein [these apply].

In the *bṛhatī* and *antara*; in the second [verse] for him; in the *madhu*, *iṣ*, and *māyā*; in the *vatsa*, *praśasā*, *viśī*, and *yajñīya*; in the *citta*, *adyā*, and *vaṃtīya*; in the *mahat*, *akran*, *vāsiṣṭha*, and *rahasya*; in the *mābhema*, *bṛhatī*, *ahi*, *svāra*, *parṇa*, *dyātaḥ*, *pārśva*, *moṣu*, *tvāyā*, *naptyoḥ*, *paripriyā*, and the two *ukta*s; in the *ūrṇāyava*, *yajñīya*, *carṣaṇīya*, *ojiṣṭhā*, *jyotis*, *aupagava*, *pavamāna*, *jījanā*, *arvāṅ*, *nilopa*, *ekaikāva*, *vite*, *śruti*, *yukṣva*, *ahikeśinā*, and on both sides.
[The word *svaḥ*] is used [as a separate word] before *prabhoḥ*, *śaikhaṇḍine*, *harivīc-*, *śākareḥ*, *ṛṣabhe*, *abhīke*, *vipaḥ*, *svarvidaḥ*, *śaṃkuni-sāhīye*, *svarvidān*,
*ārmedhe*, *nasve*, *pratyaye*, *siṣṭhatraiśokayoḥ*, and *ca*.

A *yakāra* is inserted before a vowel following words ending in *avṛddha* and others; likewise, a *vakāra* is inserted after a word-final [consonant] in all cases of "stretching" (*vikarṣa*), and there, in that junction (*sandhi*), the elision of the [preceding] vowel is prescribed at the pause (*virāma*). Such instances do not recur: in *jaṭhareṣūdvat*, *kāvavāsiṣṭhābhikrandārkeṣu*, *pṛṇaktumahām*, *itratvāṣṭrīviteṣu*, *yetvāmṛjaṃti*, *lauśaśaikhaṇḍinayoḥ*, *adarśiśrudhye*, and *vṛtreṣu*, the elision of the *luk* occurs when a double consonant follows. When a *sapta* or *he* follows a word ending in two consonants, the *luk* elision takes place.

As in *yathākāṣṭhāsu naras tvā kāṣṭhāsu*, *ārvataḥ* [is applied] when preceded by *stobha*; there is elision (*lopa*) of *u* when followed by a double consonant (*dvyanta-stha-para*), as in *yathābhīkaṣūktayoḥ aiṭate*; *tva* [is applied] in reduplication (*abhyāse*) before a suffix (*pratyaye*); *yu* and *vau* are elided after a vowel with *vṛddhi* increment (*vṛddhāt parau yvau luptau*), as in *taṃ tvā giraḥ suṣṭutayaḥ vājāya*, *tiājinn agāiḥ sūrau āktūṣu*, *ā evaṃ-jātīyāni*; *na bhūmi uccā saṃkṣāre*, *svāyudha agne sindhūnām*, *marutām dhenuḥ*, *svāsu auśane ca*, *svaśvo na kiṣṭvadrathāyām*.

In the *madas* of Priya and Asita, for Indra, for Aṣkala and Dāsa, and for the sacrifice, let there be [the Sāmans] everywhere, excluding the *bṛhadvātsapra*, *vairāja-pada-nidhana*, and *śuddhīya*. In the rivers, [there is] Priya; in the *sūnā*, the *yaudhājaya*; in the others, the *vaigaṇvatara*; in the *dharttā*, the *kāvavāsiṣṭha*; in the *abhikrandas*, the *abhikranda*; in the pressed juices, the *tvayābhūṣa*; in the *mādhucchandasa*, the *ānavaya*; in the *dyumnī* and *prahiṣṭhīya*, the *vana*; in the *aryā*, *somāya*, *āśākala*, *vārśasaṃtani*, *varṇa*, and *hare*, [these are to be applied].

In the *pṛṣṭhas*, in the *sujñāna*, in the *svādhya*, in the *somāḥ pavante*, in the *vitamadhunidhana*, in the *andhīgava*, in the *iṣejñīya*, in the *saṃvatsareṣu*, in the *prabodhiya*, in the *pravallauśasārathya*, in the *yāmīvasu*, in the *vasunyapavamānarucā*, in the *viśīya*, in the *marttyeṣu*, in the *dānāyavāryā*, in the *leya* and *śrāyantīya*, in the *kavimivāyā*, in the *auśana*, in the *vyaśnuhi-saṃkṣāra*, in the *pibātu-asyavartta-abhinidhana*, in the *ravaṃtyasya-sāmarāja*, in the *svastaye-avijñīya*, in the *dīyājñīya*, and in the *svāhutaḥ-sadudravā*.

In the *bṛhatī* and *gīthā* meters of the *vāra* and *devī* [sections], when the vowels *u*, *ū*, *i*, *ī*, *a*, and *ā* are followed by the suffixes *-hipadānta* and *-āyi*, they undergo the change to *y* in the *saṃdhi*. This applies to the *gati* [particles] at the pause (*virati*) as well as those belonging to the *āyakhya*, *indrapavamāna*, and *ābhā* [sections], as well as those of the seers (*ārṣa*). Such types [occur] in the *punānā* [section], for example: in the *gauṅgava* and *abhīvarta* [sections], in the *bhavīyasī* and *pramahiṣṭhīya* [sections], in the *ṛcaṃti*, *udvaśaputra*, *viśvānyarya*, *āparṇa*, *iṭatabodhīya*, and *ṛṣabha* [sections]; in the *indrāya*, *chaṃti*, *srucaḥ*, and *caraṃti* [sections]; and in the *naiya*, *dadhiyajñīya*, and *krauṃca* [sections].

In the *bodhīya* [section] of the *Aśvinaḥ*, there is the letter *a* followed by *ha*; O Agni, in the *aśveṣyam* [verse], there is the letter *a* followed by *sa*; in the *dairgharṣabha* [section], there are the letters *va* and *ra*; in the *jñīya* [section] of the *Śyāvāśva* [family], there is the letter *ya* following the letter *e*. In the *yāmodvatoḥ* [section], there is the letter *ga* at the end of a word (*padānta*) in the *saṃdhi*; there is the elision (*lopa*) of the letter *ya* in the *virati*; after the letter *ma*, there is the letter *yi*; after the letter *pa*, there is the letter *ri*; after the letter *ya*, there is the letter *yi*; after the letter *tra*, there is the letter *ma*; after the letter *to*, there is the letter *yi*; after the letter *e* and the letter *a*, there is the letter *go*; in some cases, after the letter *i*, there is the letter *o*; and in the case of the letters *e* and *o*, there is their unification and elision.

In the interior of a word, the *tālavya* (palatal) [nasal] occurs before a suffix beginning with *ha*, provided it is a *stobha*. It is said that there are exceptions such as *pratibhāga*, *tadāhāyi*, *papīvayaṃ*, *amṛtaṃjātā*, *vāhuṃmāyi*, and *mahāhastīdakṣāh*. Such types of cases do not apply. In the *saubhara* chant, in the verses *nahinvita*, *dyaurindrāya*, *acikramṛjyamānāya*, *agaram*, *dhrotara*, and *vājajit*, the *maṃteṣu* [nasal] occurs. In the verse *duhānāyāṃ pṛśnimantayoḥ*, they sing *tvāyāṃ* and in the *Tvāṣṭra-sāman*, the *kaniti* [nasal] occurs. In the verses *trivāvāya*, *agasaiddhukṣito*, and *śanayoḥ*, the *sadgahitta* [nasal] occurs. In the *vāra* [section], this applies everywhere within the interior of a word.

The words *nā* and *bhavati*, *svāsvābhavati* and *nimartyāt*, *vane* and *viṣṇuve*—these two words [occur] in the *Ṛṣabha-soma* hymn; *varivaḥsana* in the *Indrāya* hymn; *kautse*; *pacyadhvaryo* in the *Sāka-savīrā* hymn; *vaiśvāmitre*; *ḍinadvitīyāyām*; *tvādgarihaṃti*—and here in the *Tvaṣṭṛ-sāman*; *rabhiṃsuṣāva* in the *Soma-aurava* and the *Rahasya*; *saṃkṛtini*; *gau*; *śṛṅge*; *svarvidaḥ*; *sumneṣu*; *mānastarabhītyatra*; *jamavarttaṣedhayoḥ*; *māśivāsaḥ*; and *prahinvānaḥ*—these are the former [cases].

In the *janitre*, in the *gīrbhiḥ-uttare*, in the *śrīṇā-haviṣe*, in the *savā-jyakṣāyām*, in the *bhrave-jipavamānasya*, in the *jighratā-yām*, in the *ca-vyavadhayat-imāyām*, in the *utsedhe-hinvābhi-somāyām*, in the *tunibhiḥ-śavayoḥ*, and in the *dīrgha-niṣedhe-purojityām*, [the following applies]: in the *jambha-svarayoḥ*, there is the absence of the *anābhāva* [rule] for a palatal (*tālavya*) sound that occurs within a word (*antaḥpadika*); however, the word *dīrgha* becomes *ābhava* in *purojityām* and *jambhe-svare*. In *sahāvāt-ga-indra*, this word *eṣa* becomes *ānasta*; in *gantum-āsara*, even though it is unlengthened (*avṛddha*), it becomes *ābhava*; and in *jitīya-dīkrauñce*, [it likewise becomes so].

In the *Ṣiparītā*, there are two verses by Mādhucchandasa; in the *Varivaḥsan* for Indra, there are two by Mārgīyava; in the *Jaritṛ* and *Svara*, there are two by Parṇa; in the *Madintama*, there are two by Diṣṭha; in the *Ugihāviṣkṛta*, there is one by Yajñavābha; and in the *Vratottara* of the Aśvins, there are two.

It occurs at the end of a word in *mātegne tam adya*, *āyāṃkamaśve*, *dhmainyevāra uttare*, *jñīye syandate*, *kṛṇvate carṣaṇiḥ*, *adhītparṣi*, *hāviṣkṛte*, *varivodhāyāṃ nu*, *vyabhīnaḥ kautse*, *vṛdhesmāt piba sutāyām*, *pṛṣṭhajam avartayoḥ*, *pavantebhiḥ somāyām*, *maidhātitheniṣkṛtadgaruṇasāmnivṛṣo acikrāyām*, *parītāyāṃ ca parisrava adhisomauṣvā vāmre*, *suṣvāṇāyāṃ cāndhīgave*, *abhiprijñīye coktaḥ*, and *kṛpesvāsunaiye*.

In the *vidat* [verse] for the son of Indra; in the *udvaśīya*; in the *madhu-nidhana*; in the *tvāṣṭi-suṣvāṇā*; in the *yinta-vepur-jityā*; in the *prati-śaikhaṇḍina*; in the *pātavā-ausahita*; in the *śaṃsaya-tan-tvā-madāya-asamhita*; in the *gaviṣṭhya*; in the *ubhaya-dyu-cyāvana*; in the *diva-tvāṣṭrī-samnaḥ*; in the *sahasra-dhārā*;
in the *mādena-urvatīṣu*; in the *iti-dhyamāyā*; in the *mahānāmnī*; in the *abhiśya*; and in the *tat-id-ās-atṛtīyā*—thus ends the seventh chapter.

When the suffix *yak* occurs within a word, the *tātnavya* vowel becomes long; this applies to forms such as *vikṛṣṭastauṣe*, *mitramivaṃ prāyāsaḥ*, *viśvā tvā yāḥ*, and others of this kind. In the *naradhyaṃmahaḥ* [section], in the *anāyāṃ*, in the *kaevabṛhati*, and in the *rahasye*, and in the *bṛhati*—as in *naryaḥ sanoharīṇāyām*—and here in the *vaitre* and *vāmre*, in the *parītāyām*, in the *antyodhartāyām*, and in the *udvadbhārgava*—as in *īyastvam indra pratūrtiṣu*—it is the *abhīvarta*.

In *pīyanti* [the vowel] becomes long when followed by *abhrātṛvya*, *dvitīyāyām*, *āmahīyave*, *pīyatam*, *imān*, *aindrāyām*, *vāre*, *sphigyam*, *mābhe*, *mabṛhati*, *hīyayama*, *henoreyārvājīye*. The third [vowel] becomes long on the tongue of *ṛta* (*ṛtasya jihvāyām*). It becomes long everywhere in *jñīye*, *tvābhavati*, and at the end of a word (*padānta*) in *abhavati*. In *śarmaṇi*, *pradai*, *jñīye*, *kāṇve*, *rantā*, and in a svarita accent, it becomes long even if the preceding syllable is short (*viyastā vṛddham api*). In *priyaḥ*, *sūnuḥ*, *ṇvatare*, *saṃmīlye*, *jihyanakṛtvya*, *aśvayādhiyā*, *grahaṇādhyainauvāre*, *prathame*, *pavasvadā*, *sujñāne*, *iṅgadāśaṃkuni*, and in *viṣṭayā vācaḥ sāmni*, [the vowel becomes long].
O you two possessors of wisdom, you have established the sacrifice in heaven for the highest purpose, upon the vast expanse of the Bṛhatī, at the shore of the Kṛtvī for the sake of glory.

When the suffixes *pratyaya* are *oṃ*, *vau*, *kāra*, and when the vowels *a* and *i* are low-pitched (*nīca*) and followed by a grave (*agha*), everything becomes *vṛddhi* and there is elision of the final [vowel], as in *bharanārmedha*, *aidhmavāha*, *nihava*, *sādhr̥*, and *eṣu*. Regarding the exceptions (*apavāda*): there is *rāga* (prolongation) in *svaḥ*, *pṛṣṭha*, *naiyātithi*, and *raśmi*. In *saṃgṛbhāyā naḥ*, there is [prolongation] in *ākūpāre*; in *dūredr̥ś*, *virāṭ*, and *sudaivye*, there is the letter *t*; in *parisvānāyām*, there is the letter *m* in *aidhmavāhe*; in *kārttayaśa*, at the end, in *rāpṛcchya*, *sedhe*, *rathīnārmedhe*, and in the *prāyaścitta* formulas, [there is prolongation] in *pārthuraśme*.

In *svāsu*, excluding *āḥkāra*, there is *mokāra*; in *sakhāyaḥ* there is *so*; in *śāktye* there is *madāyatone*; in *vāyumāro* there is *bhāse*; in *mahāścarativāśe* there is *sūryamaro*; in *naiye* there is *suṣāvaso*; in *chaṃdasadvaigatayoḥ* there is *stobho go*; in *dvau gate* there is *somasu*; in *jñāne* there is *bhuvano*; in *ṛte* there is *yirno*; in *utsedhe* there is *uvarṇaṃ tu na sarvatra bhavati*; because of the mention [of specific cases], both occur; in *svāsumedhātithi* there is *naḥ*; in *suvāre prathame* there is *priyaḥ*; in *sūnurdvaigatagoṅgavayoḥ* there is *riṃdu*; in *gautamasādhrayoḥ* there is *rak*; in *siṣṭhapriye* there is *yadiṃdra*; in *citrāyāḥ* there is *śiśu*; [this applies] everywhere.

In the *ṛg-anta* [section], a contact consonant (*sparśa*), a first vowel, a *nāmin* vowel, and a *visarjanīya* do not occur; there, however, the word *auhaḥ* is extracted from the beginning. In *sadā*, *ādi*, *hvayāmaḥ*, *stiyaḥ*, and *arau*, such types [occur]. In the *daivya* [section], a contact consonant, a first vowel, a *nāmin* vowel, and a *visarjanīya* do not occur; there, however, the word *auhaḥ* is extracted from the beginning. In *avitā*, *ajarāyi*, *hṛtṝṇām*, *au*, *ā*, *hūṃ*, *mahī*, *śravasyavaḥ*, *prāyu-bhāyi*, and *rau*, the fourth [vowel] occurs. In the *devya* [section], [the word] *sacamānaḥ* occurs with the word *śiśum*.

The *samudra* [stobha] occurs at the fourth [syllable]; in the secret [portion], however, there is the *auhohāi*. At the end of a verse, there is both the *anṛganta* and the *anṛgantiya* [stobhas]. The first consonant (*sparśa*), the vowel (*svara*), the *nāmi*, and the *visarjanīya* do not occur at the end of a verse; rather, the first *kṛṣṭa-stobha* occurs precisely at the end of a verse. In the second *ilāndā*, in the third and subsequent [verses], and in the *auhovā*, the fourth *sthovṛddha* occurs at the end of every word (*padānta*). This is as in "asyaśiśum" among the Vāsiṣṭhas and in the Śyaita and Vāravatī [Sāmans]. In that regard, there are exceptions: for the *rāga* of Agni in the *Bṛhatī*, the *matsya-bṛhatī*, the *sara-pratyubṛhatī*, and the *juṣṭo agne bṛhatī*.

*yajñāṣṭāhatpūrjo ’yaṃpūṣābṛhatigāvaḥ śyenotyaḥ siṣṭhe vṛṣocāyāsyevṛṣo auhovā indroca svaḥ pṛṣṭhaiṃdo auho uvarṇaṃ tu na sarvatrābhavati grahaṇadābhavatīṃdustrikabṛhati śiśusarvatra* This [verse] begins with *yajñāṣṭāhatpūrjaḥ*, *ayaṃpūṣā*, *bṛhatigāvaḥ*, *śyenotyaḥ*, *siṣṭhe*, *vṛṣocāyāsyeva*, *vṛṣo auhovā*, *indroca svaḥ*, and *pṛṣṭhaiṃdo auho*. However, the vowel *u* does not occur everywhere; it occurs at the point of taking up (*grahaṇa*), as in *abhavatīṃduḥ*, *trikabṛhati*, and *śiśusarvatra*.

Because of the inclusion of the term *padika* ending in the vowel *ū*, it becomes *ābhavati*. [The formulas are: *namo ghovyaṃ cāgnāyiṃ namā auhovāto mā auhovā*; and the palatal [sound] following the second [consonant], as in *tālavyahāyi*. The word *śabda* also becomes *ābhavati* in the *stobha*: in the first syllable before the suffix, [as in] *śriyā ū vāhā*, *ū hā*, *ū hā hāyi svāsu nakāraḥ*, *śrāyatīye dānāyā vohudayā*, *ū vāśukāram akārau ca vṛṣṇi tsibāsu*. Everything becomes *ābhavati* in the *stobha* when there is a suffix, as in *vacanād abhan*—such types [of cases]. In *māyite vacā yā auhovā*, it is from *vānād abhā*.

Those who are indeed the two descendants of Urṇāyu, who are the two poets of great stride; those who are indeed the increasers of the sacrifice, those who are indeed the most excellent; those who are indeed active in every direction, who hear all invocations from the singers—may they be present at the end of the *kāra* syllable, for the sake of the seizers and the one-footed ones, due to the occurrence of the suffixes *kā* and *aya*, as in *kāvayām*, *avāmrasoma*, *sāmasunāmanṛtā*, and *iyamadhirāe duritāsā e suṣāho iva sāho śayeno nayā hā*.

In the *adhrigu* section, when the vowel *au* occurs as a suffix (*pratyaya*) in the word *arayiṣṭhe*, everything except for the *vṛddhi* [vowels] becomes *ā*. In the *auhaḥ-stobha* group, when there is a suffix with its own accent, the *revatī* verses are not [included]. In the *auhaḥ* [section], in the *prāṇa-rāśi-śā* and *sā-auhaḥ-neṃdra-ste-sa-na-hite*, [the rule applies]. In the *pū-viśvasya-dū-jyotiṣ-kṛṇo-va-udethā-sū-rau-gaś-ca* [sections], the sound *pu* and the sound *celāṃ* [apply]. In the *rathantara*, everything becomes *ā* except for *sparśa* (consonants) and *gabhastyo-varjo-ma-stobhe-pratyaye-aśvinor-vrata-pūrve*. And in the *tālavya-śākvara-ṛṣabhe-tvo* [sections], [the same applies].

Except for the *ṣṭhya-sparśa*, everything becomes like the *vṛṣṇi* in the case of the *ai-stobha-pratyaya*; in the case of the *vāyāmāna-pratyaya*, it is otherwise; and in the case of the *nīcādyā-pratyaya*, it is likewise.

The *ūha*, *gāna*, *yoni*, and *vatsa* notes, as well as the *stobhas*, repetitions, and pauses; repetition, praise, and meter; modifications such as the manifest (*pratyakṣa*) and the unmanifest (*parokṣa*); for these, the rule has been stated. Therefore, other [rules] depend upon those rules, as do those based on the *parvan* sections. Regarding those things which depend on the rules—just as in this case, for the four notes, the low (*mandra*), the intermediate (*atisvārya*), and the high (*uccaiḥ*), there is an interval of two [steps]; the *udvaha* is higher and higher; there is an increase in the long-drawn-out (*dīrghakarṣaṇa*) [note], and the *naṃdā* proceeds from the *sivyakarṣaṇa*; when a *gati* reaches the state of being the vowel *e*, there is the cessation of the vowel *e*; [this applies] at the end of the songs (*gītī*).

The *nidhana*s and other such elements are based on fixed rules; furthermore, those based on *parvan* (sections) have their accents established and consist of a limited number of syllables according to the meter (*chandas*). When there is an increase in the meter, an insertion (*āvāpa*) is made according to the rule; when it is decreased, there is elision from the beginning. For *parvan*-based compositions, [the rule applies] to those ending in *śurmadā*. However, for those consisting of three syllables, there is either elision of the first two syllables or no change at all in cases similar to *vāre*, *leya*, and *prastāya*. In the case of *gāyantī* and others, there is the *āṣkāra* and the *nidhana*. For *indrāyāhi* and the two following [verses], [the rule is] "we [invoke] thee" (*vayam ut tvā vat*). In the *Kākṣīvata* [hymn], there is the repetition of the vowels *ā*, *ā*, and *ya* in *uccāvad devya*. This concludes the section.

In the *vogni* and the *nidhana*, the vowel *o* is always [substituted]. In the *gauḥ-sūkta*, however, it occurs when there is an abundance [of syllables] following the *ucca* [accent]; it is obtained from the repetition of the word *ṣā*. In the *krauñca*, it occurs from the repetition of the word *hi*; in the *sāhīya*, from the repetition of the vowel *e*. Beyond this, we shall explain the modifications of the sections (*parvan*). Regarding that which is subject to the accentuation of the source (*yoni*), as follows: we shall teach by means of that very [source] whatever other section (*parvan*) occurs in a modification of the accent within the *yoni*. For example: in the *āmahīyava*, in the *madhyamā*, in the *ugra-śarma*, and in the *arari-mātṛ* verses; in these, [the rule applies] to the two subsequent ones by means of these [modifications], such as *pravai* and *indrā-māyaḥ*.

In the middle *madhyamā* [scale], however, they sang the *marāma-agniṣṭut* and the *nau-dhasa*; in the middle [scale] they should not sing the *dhājāt-svara* arising before the *prahūyasā*; and in the third [scale], the *śyaita-dhasa*, in the *anuṣṭubh*s, in the *vāyiśyetā*, in the *kāva*s, and in their own [verses], there is the addition of the vowel *a* after the word *bhiḥ*; and in the word *udapaptā* and in the word *vā*, there is always the change to *o* (*otva*) in the *pauruhanmana* hymn; they sang the *stotrā* and the *jā-svara* arising before the *tarutā*.

In the *pṛśni* [verse], in the third *dānta*, and in the *dakṣasāpati*; the *kavi* [is found] in the *pṛtārūta*, the *pati* in the *dviṣāṃ*, and the *kavyuttama* in the *jamavartta*. In the *adhyamāyāra*, *nonuma*, and *dakṣasāṃ*; the *putra* in the two following [verses], the *nemi* in the *tvannā*, and the *yaśasyuttamā* in the following [verse]. By that [verse], the *nandāmaya* in the two following [verses], the *jarisaṅghāta* in the *kārṇaśravasa*, and the *nuṣejanāsadāvṛddhā* in the *mārgīyava*. The *māgāyata* in the first *ucca*, the *prasoma* in the first [verse], the *asyapratnāt* in the two following [verses], and the *pṛṣājiga* in the first [verse].

In the *ghṛtanidhana* [sāman], there is the insertion of the vowel *svarita* after the word *anu* in the phrase *anu vaṃ*. In the *udbhava*, there is the substitution of the word *ha* for *iva*. In the *triṣṭubh* meters, such as the *supārtha*, *vārāha*, *vāsiṣṭha*, *kutsarathīya*, and others—specifically in the *vārāha*—there is *śuci vāvṛdhantā*; in the *pārtha*, however, one should substitute *vṛṇyādeḥ* with *hīṣī*. In the *dvitīya*, which is in *anuṣṭubh* meter, there is the *ṛbhusaṅghāta*. In the *mājyadoha* and *dyautānaya*, there is the *juhūsaṅghāta*. In the various meters (*vichandas*), such as the *vairāja*, *ṛṣabha*, and *ariṣṭa*, there is the insertion of *vāśedhya* at the end of the feet; and in the *dakṣasotadviṣāmatahi madge*, it is the first high-pitched syllable (*ucca*).

The first [verse] consists of four syllables; "piba somam" is the next, which possesses a womb-like [structure]. In the two following [verses], one should choose the "pāṣṭhauhī" [metre]; that is the *viviḍḍha* [metre]. In the second [verse], one should begin with "pra mahi dvitīyāyām"; "vādyadbhīryo devān" is the *viviḍḍha*. "vṛṇīmaha ā vatsaprēvṛdhaṃtādeḥ" refers to the non-extraction of that which has been extracted through drawing. In the case of the *uta* [verse], there is a repetition of the second monosyllable. But in the *kṣaudra* [verse], one should choose the first; in the *apurojyūta* [verse], there is a repetition of the three-syllable [unit] of the first [verse]. In the two *mānava* [verses], it is the former; and "dakṣasāpatiḥ kavīśurmadaścaikarcelusopāṃtyaḥ."

In this very [sequence], one should know that the penultimate syllable of the first *śurmadā*, as well as those of the *dhanya* and *tvaṣṭrī* sāmans, are low (*nīca*). Furthermore, the syllables following *dakṣasāpatiḥ*, *kavīn*, *randhra*, *uttara*, *śurmadā*, and *uttara* are high (*udātta*). One should inquire regarding the *jāta* [sāman].

One should offer the *śanaiḥ-preṣṭham* in the *āma-yoni*, and the *uṣṇih* verses in the *kūlīya*. The *vaiśvamanasa* is intended for friendship. They sing the *indrā-vaśīya* with the first *yāmā*. The two *chāhotaḥ* consist of four syllables; the latter two have three syllables, and the *chā* has five syllables. The *hotṛ* has two syllables; elsewhere, the *nidhana* is well-known as being monosyllabic. Or, in the *sāman* of the voice, it is in the *svāsu* at the beginning of the third foot of the last verse: "dakṣasota," "dviṣām," "lauśayoḥ," and "pūrve. In the *āravantā* and "viśuṣmām" in the latter [verse], the fourth [foot] is high-pitched, while the second has a short form.

Likewise, in the *aśāḥ* [hymn], the third [foot] is high; in the *plava*, the *vāravaṃta*s; in three [verses], the third foot; in the *uṣṇih*s, the second; in the four-syllable [feet], two syllables after the first; in the *janitra*s, "and *dakṣa-so-tad-viṣā-mataṃ vaḥ*"; in the third [verse], "tava māṇḍave," and in the *idāvatsara* of the *vaiṣṭha*; here itself, the third and eighth [syllables] are lengthened; in the first [verse] of the *aruṇasāman*, in the *ghṛtavatī*, in the *titheci-yoni*, the first of the two *śudhyamāna*s, the second in the *viśīya*, in the *dhaya-di-māyāṃ-bhe-pratyaya*, the first is high, and that of the last.

In the *Kavīsāhīya*, there is an increase (*vṛddhi*) or the substitution of *viṣā*; likewise, everywhere the same rule applies from the second *sakarṣa*. In the *Mandra* [section], the fourth is not a womb (*ayoni*). In the *Vaiḍaka* and *Utsa*, there is the *vasu-rūca-āyāma*; in the *Āmova*, there is the optional elision (*lopa*) of the first [syllable] in the word *aśabda*, and the substitution of *o* (*otva*) is constant in *kṣita* and in the word *hāśabda*. In the *Bodhīya*, it is taught that in *vām* there is the addition of a vowel (*svarāgama*) and the final *m*; in the *Rāga-do-viśīya*, there are the endings *-ānta* and *-āstheda*; and in the *Dau-pūrva*, there are the endings *-hānta* and *-au*.

In the *jñīya* verses, in the first [verse] of the *viśīya* group, one should choose the long vowel for the *chandaḥ* at the end of the day and night; this is the first increase established for the *viṣṭārapaṅkti*. Regarding the *kimit*, *tribṛhat*, and *devya* verses, one should choose the long vowel in the first [syllable]; according to the constant rule of the Teacher, the subsequent member is always long, as is the preceding member in the case of *vṛt*. This is the former method. In the second verse of the *śaṅku* and *eṣa* groups, there is a repetition of the letter 'a', and in the second [verse] of the *agnim vaḥ* group, there is a constant long vowel in the syllable 'e'. However, in the *aśaṅku* verses of the *Kautsa* school, the word is increased.

In the *prakṛti*, there is a long vowel in the *ūha*; everywhere in a conjunction, there is a short vowel according to the school of Ārṣa. In the *bhidrona*, *igraśarma*, and *amiṣanta* sections, it is so in the *tokā*. In that *viviḍḍhām-prāṇā*, it is so in all [verses]. In the *manājya*, *numūtaya*, and *vāyor-anīka*, it is so in the two following verses. In the four-syllable *vidhāyā* of the *yajñā-mahāmitra*, it is so in the two following verses. In the *janitre* of the two following verses, there is lengthening of the first syllable in the *udgītha* and subsequent parts of the *purojitī*. In the *danvate*, the first syllable is high-pitched (*udātta*) in the *ṛdhyava-priyā* of the two following verses. In the *vārtratūra*, the beginning of the *gītha* is high-pitched in the second [verse], and one should not sing it low in the second.

Having paused at the foot [of the verse], one should chant the *jyotis* [verse] with the *varuṇasāman* melody; the third [part] is high-pitched (*uccais*), while the fourth part, consisting of three divisions, has its *nidhana* in the middle and follows the modulations of the *nigada*. As in formal ritual application (*prayoga*), so it is in private recitation (*svādhyāya*)—except for the words *girā-girā*, *pra-pra*, *naśiṣam*, and *tasthuṣaḥ* in the *Anubrāhmaṇa* recitation. Furthermore, in the case of deity names, according to some in the *Nirukta*, the accentuation prescribed by the traditional teaching (*pravacana*) applies to both those occurring at their specific place and those occurring at other times; likewise, in the recitation of the *Śāṭyāyanins*, there is the elision of the *udātta* accent in those verses where the *udātta* occurs at the end.

In the two preceding *stotrīyas*, [the rule applies] to the penultimate word in the *mahenā*; in the *vājīya*, it applies to every *stotrīya* because of the unity of the aggregate; likewise, in the *aticchandas* verses, the *nityavat-sā* verses, and the *trika-bṛhatī*, it applies because of the unity of the section (*parva*); and in the *dimā-stoma-samanta*, it applies to the two-syllable word because of its proximity to the word-division (*pada-saṃkṛṣṭatvāt*).

The *pratistotrīya* verses, the *ārcika* sections, the *nidhanas*, and those that are constituent parts of the *stobhas* as well as constituent parts of the *parvans*; likewise, the *āhāyikāras*, the *svāpadas*, the *anusvaras*, and those belonging to the *sāmans* within [the *stobhas*], the *staubhikas*, and the *sāmāntikas*—at the end of every *sāman*, except for the *gaṇagītis* elsewhere, there is the *pratistotrīya*. For the *vodhīya*, the *dhurās*, and the two *aśvayoḥ kaṇvavṛhatīs*, the *stotrīyas* end with the *nidhana*. Everywhere, the *aiḍas* end with the *iḍās*; the *śrudhyas* end with the word "śrudhi"; the *pagavayas* consist of both *ṛc* and *sāman* and end with repetitions; and [the others] end with the *nidhana*.

In the *puṣya* and other [sections], the *ariṣṭha* [verses] end with the word *ṛk*; in the *pravad* and *udvat* [sections], they end with the word *amara*; in the *rājā* [sections], they end with the word *eka*. In the *sujñāna*, there is a *stobha* at the beginning of the *sāman*, and at the end of the *sāman*, it is according to the rule; however, in the *rahasya*, there is an extraction (*uddhāra*). This is the definition and enumeration of that [extraction]; for that which has become a limb of the *parvan*, there is no extraction. Of what is recited three times, the first utterance at the beginning of the *sāman* is as follows: in the *bhadra*, *śreyaḥ*, *riṣṭa*, *śākvara*, *ṛṣabha*, *svāśira*, *arka*, *saptaha*, and *ekavṛṣa* [sections], [the word] *śreyaḥ* [is used]. In the *ahośadva*, there is elision (*lopa*) of the *jaṃbha*, *uttaras*, *stobha*, *añjas*, and *ūrpa* [syllables].

At the end of the *sāman*, there is a word; in the *saṃskṛti* [chanting], there is a word beginning with a *stobha*. For each *stotrīyā* verse, there is a word at the beginning of the first [verse] and at the end of the last. At the beginning of the *bharga-sāman*, there is a word ending in a *stobha*. In the *vairāja* [chanting], the word "ṛṣabha" occurs at the end of the final [verse]. Just as in a village there is the sequence beginning with "vairājaiya," so too at the end of the *stotrīyā* verses, in all [verses], there is a syllable at the beginning of the *stotrīyā* joined with the word "matsva."

The Ājyadoha hymns are in reverse order; for the first of these, the initial word at the beginning of the Sāman undergoes no modification, as do the *ātharvaṇa*, *devasthāna*, *svara*, *antarikṣa*, *tauraśrava*, and *māna* syllables. There is an extraction (*uddhāra*) of all [syllables] except for the Vairūpa, but in that case there is no extraction of the names of the deities. For the sake of the successful performance of the ritual, here [in the case of] the *iḍā*s and the *ekavṛṣa*, the name of the deity is [retained]; however, the *nidhana* occurs at the end of the Sāman everywhere, whichever is shorter.

In the *guru* [stotras], there is a single portion of the *niṣadha*; in the case of the three recitations, the final word; but in the *ṛṣabha*, that which is recited thrice; in the two preceding the *devasthāna*, the first part of the *nidhana*; in the last [recitation], the entire [text]; in the *divākīrtya*, the *vairāja*; in the *bhrāḍvikarṇa*, the *ṣṭhā-svara*; in the *ambhāsa*, the hundred [syllables]; in the *ādiyaśas*, the seven causes; in the *āgha-vacana-sāman*s, the first word beginning with *ape-graha*; in the *apāvṛt* and *gavām-vrata*, the *kvavānta* [syllable] at the beginning; in the *aśvinor-vrata*, the vowel *ī* preceded by the *vrata*; in the *atikrānta*, the *vairūpa*, *śārkvara*, and *ṛṣabha*, the half-verse ending in *iḍā*.

At the end of the *sāman*, there are two *stobhas* for the *Aśvavrata*: *au-hau-hyau-hau-hau*. There are four *somās*, or *au-hau-vātsīs*, or *svar-jyotis*. The first *uccha* begins with the syllable *ekāra*; thus are the *padas* and *stobhas*. In the subsequent *vidhās*, the *pāda-gīti* is the same: *jyotir-bhāḥ śiśur vājy aśvo medhyaḥ*. The extraction (*uddhāra*) is in the latter two; at the end of the *sāman*, there are *stobhas* for the *nidhana*, namely *svarvataḥ*. The *nidhana* consists of the *upagraha* and so forth. These are the five *vyātdṛti-sāmans* in these [verses]: *bhūr bhuvaḥ svar satyam puruṣaḥ*.

The *pṛthak* [chant] has Agni as its *dūta*; the *tāva* is low-voiced; Soma is recited three times in the *ānīkayā*; the third [part] is the *svarjyotis* finale; the *ekāra* at the beginning is unaccented (*akṛṣṭa*). In this manner, for all [chants], this rule of modification (*vikāra*) applies. By this method, the collection of *sāman*s should be adapted, should be adapted.
Thus ends the eighth chapter.

Now, regarding the variations of the *vikalpa* (optional) *svarita* accents: in the *madamado-dhana-kāma*, in the *puraḥ-svāsu*, in the *uttarayoś-cāraṅga-mānade*, in the *aṣṭeḍarayiṣṭhayoḥ*, in the *hinvanādīdihisvarā*, in the *mātāvṛddhaśvāmitre*, in the *kraudhyamaṣaṣṭhannavamātraṃ dīrgheparayoḥ*, in the *doṣāparannīcairgavatṛtīyadaśamaṃ kṛṣṭa*, in all cases of *dharmavidharmaṇoḥ*, in the *pañcākṣaraśodhanāni*, in the *stāve*, in the *haviṣa uttarayoḥ*, in the *prathame*, in the *virāṭparyūca*, in the *devyegītha*, in that beginning with *nava*, in the *nihotā*, and in the *nidhātuvārā*.

In the *tveṣa* [hymn], the long *ga* occurs; in the *āsophatṛtīyā*, there is a floating [of the syllable] with *ṛtena* as the base, and it is submerged in the middle like a lotus. At the end of the two [verses], there is elision of the *va*, and the *ta* is high-pitched; in the *yajivāha*, it floats here in the *ā*. In the subsequent [verses], *agnim dūtāstāva* is in the *ṇvabṛhatī* meter, and the chant is "udā ā". In the *ṣabhekāmpā*, *tvaṃ no vāre* is in the *punāṇvabṛhatī*; in *prasoṇvatare* and *punābhisojaṃbhe*, there are variations in the two subsequent *kakubh* meters.
Now we shall explain the *bhāvas* by which the *pragāṇa* (chanting) is prescribed.
Those by whom the *ārcika* and *staubhika* verses are altered—
whether in their *āyitva*, *prakṛti*, *vṛddha*, or *avṛddha* forms,
as well as the *gatāgata* of the *stobhas* and likewise their high and low pitches.

Understand that in the *ūha* [of mantras], there is singing like *saṃdhi*, like words, and likewise the state of being *ātman* or *arbha*; furthermore, there are conjunctions (*praśleṣa*) and disjunctions (*viśleṣa*),
as well as the consonant being drawn together (*saṃkṛṣṭa*), drawn apart (*vikṛṣṭa*), elided (*lupta*), or unaltered (*anikṛta*).
One should observe the states (bhāvas), the modifications (vikāras), and the utterances (ūha) within the emotional states;
for it is through these states that all the various Vedic branches sing individually,
yet they mostly sing within the five breaths and the musical notes (svaras).
The Sāmans are [recited] in six ways, while others are in seven; however, the Kauthumas [use] two.

For those deficient [verses], there is a different chanting; and as for those additional quarters which are seen in the source (yoni), they are equal, whereas other quarters are equal syllable by syllable.

The state of coming (āyibhāva) does not exist now; that which is drawn out long indeed ceases when the drawing is completed. In the case of an affliction (*upadrava*) involving both *āyi* and *bāya*, both states are observed in the *sāman* according to their respective order.
In all cases, one should perform the *ūha* (modification) by means of *abhyudūha*; the singing is like that of a secret [text].
In the first section (*parvan*) beginning with *svā*, as well as in other *sāmans*, whether it be the syllable of the *ārcika* according to the rule for the *nidhana*, or that of the *staubhika*.
The drawn-out and the not-drawn-out shall be the noble accent; for growth, the final syllable is acute.
He who sits among the stones, the one who enters the un-yoked, the seeker of what is desired, the conqueror—through you, he attains the beloved, the one who bestows strength and overcomes the enemy.
Just as the son of Adharma, Udvya, was honored by the seers,
so too do these [qualities] depart from the right path; some [speak] for the sake of increase,
while others, like Bhāsa, Pauṣkala, Aṣṭeḍara, and Ariṣṭha, are most intent on the destruction of dharma.
In the *traita*, *aśva-vrata*, *śaukta*, *andhīcit*, and likewise in the two *ṣaḍṛca*s, there are six;

in the *pauṣkala* and *ṣaṣṭha-ṛca*, seven; in the *rayi-śaukta* and *vṛṣāstobha*, three; in each of the *anyāya-virodhinī* and *tṛca*s, two; and in the *aśva*, *andhīgava*, *stobha-dharma*, and the five *acchidra*s, [the same applies].

In the *stobha*, the third and penultimate syllable becomes long, except in the *vāmadevya* and in the *kautsa* where it ends in a consonant; furthermore, the vowels *i* and *u* do not [become long] in the *adhvaryava*, nor in the middle of the *sana*, nor in the *indrāyāṃ*, nor in the *kṣaudra*, nor when followed by *kṛta*, nor at the end of a word in the *viśīya*, nor in the *pūrva-śūṣa*, nor in the *triṇidhana*, nor in the *āyāsya*, nor in the *sedheṣiṇodana*, nor in the *kāma*, nor in the first section of the *sauma-stāva*, nor in the *kārtā*, nor in the *paryaśvin*, nor in the latter part of the *nārvrata*, nor in the *śaṅku* where there is the vowel *e*, nor in the *ṛṣabha*, nor in the *śākvara*, nor in the *saṃmīlya*, nor in the *laghu-vinata*, nor in the *atve*, nor in the *kāleya*, nor in the *pratna-mahīyava*.

And in the *krauñcābhinidhana* [sāman] on the seven-day [rite], in the *uttaradharta*, *udvat*, and *rāsadasyu*, in the *pūrva-vṛṇyādi-jiteśva*, in the *asaṃyoga* with *mapottara* as the *stobha*, in the *krauñca* when there is no *saṃyoga*, in the *kautsa* where the word "hi" occurs, in the *pravat* of *bhārgava*, in the *kṛṣṭha-ādasthāt* where the vowel 'a' occurs in the *svāra*, in the *parṇa* beginning with "hā," in the *yonis* of "tvat," in the first *aṅga* of "gahya," in the second *aṅga* ending in "santaḥ," in the "santaḥ" of *ṣañja-mitrera*, in the *vratas* of *rathantara-vṛṣāśvinau*, in the *dairgha* without a *stobha*, and in the two following [sections] of the *vrātya*.

In the *thelāndatīyayaukta* [verses], there is the vowel *au*; in the *stāvādya* [section], the first [syllable] in the *kaṇvatareva* [group]; between the *anekṛṣṭa* and *vṛddhi* [sections], the *vṛṇyādi* [syllables] in the *raivata*; in the *sāhīya*, the second ending of the word *śatāyās* due to its being *tat*; in the *sapra* [section], the first syllable of *sūryasya* in the *mrebhisāma*; the last [syllable] of the first [verse] in the *bodhīya*; in the *madhu* [name-section], according to some, the word *devya* in the *edīdhinvavāvitadevya* [group]; the word *tsya* in the two *svaras*; the distinction of the *kubheda*; and the lengthening [of the vowel] with *śyenena*.

In the Śākta [Veda], the word *īṣyant* is [used]; in the Vṛddha [Veda], *śataplava*; in the Vārānta [Veda], *uṣatayaś*; and in the Danvata [Veda], *vipra*. In the Hayistāvat [Veda], words ending in a vowel (*svaranta*) are used; in the Naga [Veda], words with *śū* as an upadhā; and in the Upadhrī [Veda], words ending in *tvāṣṭrī*. In the Sāmnihāra [Veda], words beginning with *yoni* are used. There are nine [words] in the Pūrvapajra [Veda]: *aruṇa*, *sāma*, *aśoka*, and *pṛśni*. In the Noda [Veda], the words *irikte* and *ariṣṭe* are used; in the Śabda [Veda], the two words *ye* and *vī*; in the Samudra [Veda], the word *chandasi*; and in the Utāyā [Veda], the second [word] is *amarapavirāja*. In the Tāvādreṣṇa [Veda], words that are not vṛddha are used; in the Saṃkṣāra [Veda], *vaiśvajyautiṣa*; and in the Gorāgirasa [Veda], words ending in *ni* are used. In the Odejya [Veda], [the following applies].

In the *vyedri*, *tejaya*, *triṇidhana*, and *sāptamika* [sāmans], the deity is Sārvādi; in the *siṣṭha*, in that which has *viviḍḍha* as its final *yoni*, and in the *ruṇasāman*, [the deity is] Rūpado; in the *viśīya*, *aṣṭiḍa*, and *ūrmiṇa*, [the deity is] Udbhāja; in the *jambha*, the third [syllable] begins with *d*; in the *nitra* and the first *deviśīya*, it begins with *h*; in the *śṛṅga* and *kautsa*, it is *vesūṣvā*; the fourth [syllable] is at the end of the *ekonā*; the final syllables of the *rādhā* increase; in the two following [sāmans], in the *catirothatyā*, and in the first [sāman] like the *yoni*, it is at the end; in all [these], it is for the *ghṛtanidhana*, and in the *śūvatyā*.

In the *mantavaddānti*, here [is] another; in the *śāvivonāyām* and the first part, due to the extraction of the syllable, in the second *mantra*, on the day, and not for Rāhu, in the third, the slayer of the gods, from the tree, the glory of the descendant of Vasiṣṭha, and the lord of the two enemies, the wise one, this Dāsa, in the latter two, the third, from the high, the origin of the *ṣkala*, in the *jāsvara*, in the *upaśikṣā*, of the *prāvṛṣahūyasā*, in the *kreṣvāyāsye*, in the passage "punānaḥ," here the Soma, the syllable, the increase, the *ai* vowel, toward Indra, in the two-syllabled [verse], at the beginning, "mīḍhe," the high, the low, the double-high, the father, the *pavamāna*, the *āśivāsaḥ*, and these, in the fourth, the *śava*, the *avapām*, the *indra*.

The first [part] of that [Sāman] consists of the *haduktha* form; the second is that which has been transgressed and reached, and is sung with the *bhīśava*, *gataśyaita*, *jigottara-yoni*, *trasvāra*, *yāma*, *aiṣira*, *vāma*, *aurṣāhara*, *vācaḥsāma*, *hakta-priya*, *agṛra-misni*, *dunva*, *nnapokṣa*, and *bodhīya* verses; all [of these] in the *ayoni*, *nitra*, and *viṣa* meters, in the *gītha*, *pravājya*, and the two *uttara* sections, in the *steya-nidhana*, *ābhihita*, *pauṣkala*, *havyagāra*, *mānava-vantīya*, *bhara*, and *parṇaya* chants.

Now follows the rule for the *u* sound: when it is long by nature (*prakṛtyā*), its occurrence as a non-final syllable (*apadāntaḥ*) and when it is identical (*samānam*) [to the following vowel] is subject to the option (*vikalpe*) of nasalization (*narave*). Examples include: *priyāvasu sisīdatu*, *bhūriteva sunasantaninidhanatvāt somyam madhu*, *vyokāraḥ pādamadhye*, *thendo babhro retare vasor vasūni*, *dānte yahodhrigos tāve indram va*, and *ukāra urāvimomadhau matautasthau yonau cābhe*.

In the *rathantara* [sāman], the first [syllable] is high-pitched (*udātta*) in the first verse; everywhere else, the fourth syllable is low-pitched (*anudātta*), as is the *ma* syllable in "na jāto dabhraḥ" and "sudevo vaḥ. In the *ṣedha*, the third and fourth syllables of "deduri tāvasat" are high-pitched. In the *ājāvit*, the two following [syllables] in "endrayāhi" are high-pitched, while in the two preceding ones and in "paryūṣu," the penultimate syllable is high-pitched. In the *patiṃ girā*, the first two syllables are high-pitched; in "site" and in the first two of "devādyayoḥ," the third syllable is high-pitched. In "abhisomādyayoḥ," "pibāsu," and the first of "nadevasvāsvādyayoḥ," the fourth syllable is high-pitched. In the *yathāyoni*, the first syllable is high-pitched in the second verse, and the first in the first.

In the *nighāta* (unaccented) syllable, in the third [verse], and in the two thirds; in the *kaulma*; in the *iṣṭā*, *asikṛṇuṣṭām*, and *āśubhārgave*; when there is an elevation (*udātta*) of three syllables, or an elevation of five syllables, in the first two [verses]; like the *yoni*; in its middle [verse]; in the *ātūna*, *ākūpāra*, and *ca*; in the first [verse]; in the two following [verses] of two syllables; in the *acchidra-ekarca*; the low [pitch] (*anīcaḥ*); the word *śetaḥ*; and in the absence of *vṛddhi*; in the suffix *vice*; in *vṛddha-sita*; in *vṛṇyantaḥ*; the final syllable of the second *pāda* of *kṣīvate*; the non-second vowel; in *viśīye*; not elevated at the beginning; low [pitch] in *nau*; in all *jñīya-ṛk*s; in the first [verse].

The other [stotras] are like those of the *jñīya*; the third is drawn once; for the two following [stotras], the second is [drawn] twice; and when there is a *ṇidhana* on a single syllable, the second [verse] is used in the *jaya*.

The Hotṛ shall sacrifice with the *gūrda* and the two following [verses] according to the *jñīya* rule. In the *prastāva*, at the *yoni*, and at the *sadhastha*, he should perform the *yajis* as if they were a collection; likewise for the *pūrvārka*, *puṣya*, and *rayiṣṭha*. He should take up the *staubhika* sections. At the end of the *sāman*, all [elements] are [performed]; in the *ārcika*, in the *akṛṣṭa*, and everywhere except at the *yoni*, in the *vaidhṛta*, in the *ṣṭha*, *nau*, *the*, and *re*, the second [part] is [performed]. In the *vāmnī*, except at the *yoni*, in the *chidra*, in the *abhisomādyāyānī*, in the *nīcaṃdhyabhyāsa*, and in the *jñīya-ṛk*s, [the rule applies]. In the *viśīya*, at the final *ādga*, and in the *syāmā* and *mābha*, because of their oneness, there is the *mābhāsa*.

In a word consisting of two vowels, there is a pause; some say this also applies to the *ṇvu* suffix and in the *abṛhatī* chant. After a hundred [syllables], there is a pause for the *mā*, *bhaya*, *uñjoḥ*, *upadhyamāyāmuḥ*, *sthamāu*, and *vāyāṃ*. In the third foot of a *ḍin* verse, there is a pause after *agastau* and *abhyāsāt*; some say this also applies to the *arbha* and *raṃ* in a sonorous (*ghoṣa*) passage. Regarding the *visarjanīya*, it is established by tradition (*āmnāya*). In the *bahatī* and *krauñca* chants, in the third foot, there is a high pitch (*ucca*) as in the *abhīvarta* chant, and likewise in the third foot of the *dadadrāṇa*. In the *rakṣāśata* and *uṣvepatiḥ* verses, as well as in the *kavīṣu* verses, there is a repetition (*abhyāsa*) of the final syllable. In all [verses], in the third foot, there is a *vīta* between the *kṛṣṭa* and the *vṛddhi*.

Fame is lost and infamy arises; for those who possess good conduct, there is the loss of life in the presence of serpents. The two sounds *vānti* and *eti* are base; he delighted in everything, yet he is not seen by the sun. This is known as *hammā*, like salt and other substances in the horn of a cow. In the case of *saṃjaya*, *bhīśava*, *vaiyaśva*, and *sādhrādi*, because it is established by its own characteristic, there is one joint in another substance. Like *leya* in the *chāyantīya*, there is a pause in the *marāya*; it is drawn out in the *vairāja* when there is no womb (*ayoni*). However, in the *vairūpa*, there is a prohibition against bowing; rather, the word for the deity is placed at the *nidhana*.

In *agne* [there is] *striṇidhana*; in *uṣvāyām*, the second [occurrence] in the second foot; in *govatyām* and *ānīkapāyām*, the first; in *nuṣmi* and *śoke*, *pra* and *svare*; in *thā uttare*, *dadgaṣṭre*, and *sośabde*, [the same]; in *dāse*, *dukthe*, *abhigīta*, and *krama*, [the same]; in *aharya medhe*, after the *hāyi-stobha*, the third; in *ayonau*, in *kāve*, in the *gītha-ṣaṣṭha*, everywhere [the same]; in *añja*, the fifth; in *pro ayāsyāt*, the seventh; in *tvāṃdūta* and *udapaptayāḥ*, in the *vairāja*, the *pra* and *sa* sounds have turned back; in the *vairāja*, the *pra* and *sa* sounds have turned back—thus ends the ninth chapter.

The syllable *na* occurs as a *sandhyagīta* (conjunct chant) in *kuvitsunāyām*, *bodhīye*, and *ihavaddaivodāse*; and as the first [syllable] in *uttamāyām aprathamaḥ svāsu*, *sāhīye*, and *uttamāyām abhisomādhyāsyāyādga*. Everywhere in the *yoni*, in *dvīḍe dhartādvyakṣaraṃ parva*, it is drawn toward the first vowel because of the following *udghāta* (accentual break), due to being deficient by one syllable and because of the presence of an additional verse-division (*parva*). In *abhipri*, all [syllables] are three-syllabled in all [verses], except for the second and fourth quarters; in *marāye*, there is a repetition (*abhyāsa*) of a single syllable at the end of a three-times-stated quarter. Everywhere, except before *puraḥ*, there is a repetition of the particle *hi* in the middle of the quarter.

[The syllable] *om* occurs before *preddha*, *agre*, *dīdihi*, *gūrda*, and *vṛddha*; [the syllable] *hi* occurs at the beginning of a word when followed by the suffix *agni*; [the syllable] *o* occurs in the *sāhīya*, *mahīyava*, and *kaulma* chants, as well as in the *dāsa* chant; [the syllable] *o* occurs in the *kāvaparṇa* and *kūlīya* chants and in the *sāhīya* chant; [the syllable] *bhi* occurs in the *anutkāva* chant; [the syllable] *o* occurs in the *nādhvatavat*, *aparṇa*, and *bodhīya* chants, and in the *vāci* chant everything becomes *o*; [the syllable] *o* or *u* occurs in the *anusthoma* chant; [the syllable] *tu* occurs in the *aparāyā* chant; [the syllables] *anātṛtīyam*, *kṛṣṭam*, and *pratyutkrāntam* occur up to the fourth *kṛṣṭa*; [the syllables] *tu* and *pādānte* occur in the *mandrakṛṣṭa* and *amandrakṛṣṭa* chants; [the syllable] *vṛdhe* occurs from the words *vyajñānāt* and *ga sanitya*.
Furthermore, there is a repetition by another in the case of *daivya* and *aurṇāyava*.

There is a *yakāra* in the word *sānu*, and everywhere in the case of *ākāra*. In the *bodhīya* and *nidhana*, and in the case of a sonant (*ghoṣa*), [the rule applies] to *trī*, *krauñca*, *pramaśāktya*, *asaṃjaya*, *bharakraṃda*, *abhikārṇa*, *śravaśya*, *etākūpa*, *viśovibhīśaka*, *kubha*, *svāra*, *parṇaśva*, and so forth. In the case of *āyāsya*, *dvini*, *kāṇva*, *kārtayava*, *śyāvāśva*, and *yaśva*, they are to be understood as being accompanied by the middle [pitch], provided they are not *anidhana* or *dgrahīṣya* among the *sāman*s.

In the *Śyaita*, the third [syllable] and those following it are high-pitched (*udātta*), except for the third which is low-pitched (*anudātta*); this applies to the two final [verses]. In the *Bṛhatī*, from the *Candrā*, in the second [verse], the *ekadga* is everywhere to be observed; in the first and third [verses], the *iyasūcā* is low-pitched for that duration. In the third [verse], the first [syllable] is low-pitched; in the first *āyā*, the first [syllable] is low-pitched; in the second *āyā*, the *tamasa* is low-pitched; in the second *ekadga*, it is everywhere in the *ayoni*. In the first *de*, in the *stobha*, and in the subsequent [verse], the letter *o* becomes *va*. In the *hiṣṭhīya*, *gava*, and *vasita*, the *saca* is everywhere in the *ayoni*. In the *vasucaddhi*, in the second *dasu*, in the third [verse], and in the first *yonau*, in the *jayeca*, the *stāvā* is in the *ayoni*.

In the *krauñca* [chanting], from the first *ucca*, for those who are *sūra*s, and from the third *geṣṇa*, the third [syllable] is not elided. From *indra* there is *āyi*; from *tājja* there is elision; and from *dviṣāyāśca* there is *adyaśravā*. He should protect the *gayā*s; from the ancient *pīyūṣa* there is *yāyāg*. In *satrādyasya* there is elision; in *kṛti* there is the third [syllable]; in all these cases, *ramya* is employed. In the *anuṣṭubh*, in the second and sixth [verses], prior to the four [syllables], in the *ayoni*, "om" is low-pitched. In the third *śveta*, in the *pṛṣadvareka-ṛc*, in the two *vedasa-jñīya*s, and in the *hārādyoni*.

In the *daviṣṭhā*, *uttamāyāt*, *gasoma*, and others, as well as in the *āgneyī* and *jāsvara* [verses], there is the *vṛnnaviṃchada* [modification] in the *prahūyasāyāt* and other [cases]. In the *yakṣara* [verses], there is the *avṛddādistani* [modification] on both sides. According to the verse, the *gas* [modification] applies everywhere in the *astāva* and *hāra*. In the *avaśye*, *hi*, *stoma*, *sumarā*, *apramarājī*, and *care*, the *bhe* [modification] occurs. In the *cākārānta* [verses], there is the *krānta* [modification]; in the *mayo*, there is the *nā* [modification], and in the *udūha*, it applies everywhere. In the *mīḍhe*, there is the *gateḥ* [modification], and in the *kanīyasi*, there is the *atvam* [modification] of the syllable *o*. Because of the established rule that the *tvam* [modification] does not apply when the word is sung (*padagīta*).

Listen to these [verses]: in the fourth [chapter], they are to be recited everywhere; in the third [chapter], they belong to the *saṃvatsara* (year-long rite); and in the first [chapter], they belong to the *gomadaśva* (the one rich in cattle). From Indra [come] the Maruts; in the last [verse], he bestows [them]. From the fourth [chapter] onwards, they are to be joined according to their source (*yoni*). In the second [chapter] of the *Gastava*, there is the *ghātadgaruṇasāman*; however, in the first and last [verses], there is a modification (*vikāra*). In the *Nārmedha*, there is *dhā* at the beginning and end. Protecting the *upāmā* (near limit), it becomes *thamaḥ*. In the *Ṛṣabha-havimajana*, there is *bhulaṃvismiṃtsica-varupṛṣṇi-śyaitamadgeṣu ṣṭaṃbhecauśasūye śīye ca*. In the *nākṛt*, there is *daga*; in the *hyaśas*, from the *kṛṣṭā* [comes] one.

In the *dhayamāya*, the letter *a* is mixed with the second *ga*; in the *surūpa*, the *pada-gīta*, and the *oṣṭhya*, the letter *ha*; and in the *marāya*, the letter *ka* both become two-mora (*dvimātra*). In the *tarāya*, the letter *ṣṭha* is applied; in the *nau-varuṇa-sāman*, in the second *lāṃde*, in the *tha-mocca*, and in the *ūbhāti*; and in the fourth, in the *vṛṇījā-svara-ga*. Everywhere, the *kāṃpā* is also applied; in the *nayata-vig-na-ireca*, in the *dedeca-vidhāḥ*, everywhere in the *yoni*, in the *jā-svara-ga*, in the *manasa*, and in the *dviṣaśva-manasa*.

In the *apsuṣada* [section], within the *īkṣā*, there is a *nidhana* like that of the *kāraṇidhana* at the penultimate [verse]; the *abhyāsa* (repetition) consists of five syllables, except where it is omitted after the *suta*. In the *krāyā*, in the *rājedhyamāyāṃpāṣṭe*, and in the *vṛdādyāyāṃcāṃtyasyattamase*, in the two following [verses], in the *vṛṇīta*, and in the *rutecaturakṣare*, there is no repetition (*abhyāsa*). In the *narāyehā*, from the second [verse] onwards, it is drawn once; from the end, the *vidhā*s are everywhere in their own [verses], and in the last [verse], in the first *de*, the final [consonant] is a retroflex (*mūrddhanya*), followed by a vowel, and the *ṇa* becomes *ya*; in the *hārī*, it remains as it was originally, like an unmodified preceding word; and in the *pariṣkṛta*, the augment (*āgama*) is to be elided.

In the *vya* of the *kārṇaśravasottara*, [the *daga*] is in the *svadayasadāvṛdhāṃ*; the *dasmaḥ* is in the *surākrauca*; the *astrabhāna* is in the *hi vā*; [the *daga*] is in the *agni vā*; the *vājīya* is in the *upāṃttya*; the *kṛṣṭa* is in all [verses] of the *trikavat-sā*. In the first and second [of these], the fourth [verse] is [the *daga*]; in the two following, the fifth; in those [verses] of the *vairāja* [meter], the third; in the *vṛddha* [verses], the first and last; in the *aprasa*, the *nārmeda*, the second [verse]; in the *rādhā*, the third; in the *ayoni*, the *kautsa*; the *daga* is in the *aṣṭra-uttara-kūpāra*; the *śrudhya-pṛśni-māna* is in the first [verse]; and in the *aruṇa-vaidhṛta-vāsiṣṭa-tithakubha-nitra*, it is in the *canas*.

The first [verse] of the *tīṣaṃga* and *śākvara* [sāmans] is chanted on non-yoni verses; [the verse] *agnisvāvṛdhaḥ* is used for the *riṃu*; *ayi śoke* with the *maṅga*s for the *triṇidhana*; and for the latter two of the *sauhaviṣa*, [the verses] *go*bhiḥ and *ilāndasva* are used, the last and the penultimate being on non-yoni verses.

He who takes away the earth with the Śyena-sacrifice; he who dug out the firm [earth] with the Vārāha-sacrifice; the second plowing was for the sake of wealth; he who milked the four-syllabled [verse] from the divine cow; in the second [part], the Vairāja [melody] is chanted on the two final syllables; [the Sāman] belongs to Viśvamanas due to the taking of the *graha* at the junction of the *stobhas* and the *ṛc*; it is joined with the second ending; in the first [part] of the Śaukta, and in the first two of the Śaukta, there is the "well-mixed" (*suṣāśrīṇa*) [chanting]; in the Āruṇasāman, the *ilā* [verse] beginning with *dehi* is the extraction (*uddhāra*), while in the last [verse] there is no extraction;
in the *tamasoḥ* [Sāman], there is the raising (*udghāta*) and the lowering (*nighāta*) in the first two [verses] of the Māgāyata.

Now follows the summary of the introductory sections (*prastāva*) for these various chants (*gītis*): the *stobha* occurs either before, within, or after the *prastāva*. For the *udgātṛ*, it consists of the syllables *takāra*, *ṛṣabha*, *pāvamāna*, and *janitra*; or it begins with *hu* in the *vāsiṣṭa* hymns. In the absence of a specific instruction, it is two syllables long; however, for the *saṃkṛti*, *dārḍhacyuta*, *surūpa*, *ajīgaḥ*, *aiḍa*, and *sākamaśva* chants, it is four syllables long. For the *rājana*, *śākvara*, and *ṛṣabha* chants, it is two syllables long. For the *saṃjaya*, *anada*, *gośṛṅga*, *rātri*, and *daivodāsa* chants, it is likewise [four syllables].

The *kāva*, *śrautakakṣa*, *ārṣabha*, *bhartṛ*, *atāyāsya*, *aiḍa*, *aukṣṇa*, *aurandhra*, *aiḍasāuparṇa*, *autkṣamārgīya*, *vajrarābodhīya*, *yadvāhiṣṭhīya*, *utsedha*, *vāmra*, *svāra*, *sāmarāja*, *paurumīḍha*, *pūrvavāravaṃtīya*, *vārtraturayaṇa*, *vairūpa*, *hrasvābṛhat*, *opaśa*, and *mahādivākīrttya* chants; the wind from the ploughed field, the *vṛṣṇi* twice, the *vāravaṃtīya* in the self, the *mahādivākīrttya*, the *yāntodāśasyanti*, *abhāsa*, *śāṃmada*, the *gāyatrī*, the *asita*, the *jārānta*, the *vīṅka*, and those of *vasiṣṭha* and *priyapajra*.

The *vārānta* [Sāmans] belong to Vaiśvāmitra; those ending in *hāukāra* belong to Saṃtanin; those ending in *jamadagni*, *abhīvarta*, *kārtayaśa*, and *kārānta* belong to Tvaṣṭṛ; and those beginning with *jāra*, *agni*, and *dūta*, as well as those that are indivisible (*avibhāgya*), [belong to the same].

The two-syllable [words] of Yauktāśva, Aiḍayāsya, Traiśoka, Krośaśnu, Auṣṭodvadaśa, Putra, Dīrghatamas, Simāna, Niṣedha, and Vairāja; the two-syllable [words] of Ānṛpa, Eta, Sāhaviṣa, and Vaiṣṇava ending with *payas*; the twelve-syllable [words] of the Svaras beginning with Agnidūta, the repeated middle [verse] of Krauñca, the repeated [verses] ending in *vaṣaṭ* of Kūpāra, Rājan, and Payas; and the three-syllable [word] of Carāvarta in the Ṛṣabha-Bṛhatka.

The Soma-sāman, Gāyatrī, Krauñca, Vairūpa, Audala-gāyatrī, Auśanasa, Aindukṣita, Mādhātitha, Rohitakūlīya, Havirdāna, Aindhmavāha, Indrayaśas, Kaṇva-bṛhat, Traiṣṭubha, Śyāvāśva, Śauktavārṣāhara, Vājabhṛt, and Kārṇaśravasa—of these there are four [stobhas], or two at the end of each; six for Śaṅku, Bārhata-vājajit, Svāra, Rohitakūlīya, Asitayauktasnuva, and Aurukṣaya; eleven for the Jāgata Soma-sāmans; twelve for the Hariśrī; and they end with the stobha upāyāntaḥ.

In the *padanidhanas*, that *nidhana* belongs to the *gadgada*; it occurs twice in the *ekavṛṣa* and thrice in the *padastobhas*. In the *ilā* and others, it is recited three times as prescribed; in the others, it is at the end, consisting of two syllables. In the *mahānāmnyas*, the *dvipadās*, the *śākvaras* with the first [verse], and the *adhyāsa-purīṣas*, it is as taught. In the *vaichaṃdasas*, the singing is exactly like the introductory (*prāstāvika*). The subsequent verses of the *yaṇvādis* are not subject to the *prastāva*; or rather, the *asaṃtaninas* are subject to the *prastāva*. "The *asaṃtaninas* are subject to the *prastāva*"—thus ends the tenth chapter of the *Puṣpasūtra*.
The Puṣpasūtra is completed;
thus the Sāmaveda Prātiśākhya is completed.
